source_description: Financial entities shall implement the rules laid down in Chapter II in accordance with the principle of proportionality, taking into account their size and overall risk profile, and the nature, scale and complexity of their services, activities and operations.
addendum:
Missing specification(s) in the CCM v4.1: 
"the principle of proportionality, taking into account their size and overall risk profile, and the nature, scale and complexity of their services, activities and operations."
analysis:
Not identical or equivalent. Compared proportionality concept in DORA to risk-based references in CCM. Not fully identical so there are some gaps. DORA's proportionality specifically links to "size and overall risk profile" as measurable criteria, which is more prescriptive than CCM's general risk-based approach.

It is assumed that "proportionality" as referred to in DORA is broadly similar to "risk" and "risk based" as referred to in CCM. Companies should note, however, that not all references to "proportionality" in DORA have an exact equivalent in CCM and or do not always refer to "risk" and "risk based" in CCM. At a headline, one can make compliance equivalence assumptions but note there may be some gaps. See examples below.

CEK-09: Proportional auditis regarding encryption. Not equivalent. Not comparable.
HRS-01: Background screening policies and procedures proportionate to data classification. Not equivalent. Not comparable.

source_description: In addition, the application by financial entities of Chapters III, IV and V, Section I, shall be proportionate to their size and overall risk profile, and to the nature, scale and complexity of their services, activities and operations, as specifically provided for in the relevant rules of those Chapters.
addendum:
Missing specification(s) in the CCM v4.1: 
"shall be proportionate to their size and overall risk profile, and to the nature, scale and complexity of their services, activities and operations."
analysis:
CCM lacks a framework-wide proportionality mechanism that allows controls to scale based on entity size/complexity. It is assumed "proportionality" as referred to in DORA is broadly similar to "risk" and "risk based" as referred to in CCM. Companies should note, however, that not all references to "proportionality" in DORA have an exact equivalent in CCM and or do not always refer to "risk" or "risk based" in CCM. At a headline level, one can make compliance equivalence assumptions but note that there may be some gaps depending on the specific issue being considered.

DORA Article 4 is describing the principle of proportionality for the entirety of the control to be applied. The controls in CCM CEK-09 and HRS-01 are not equivalent or comparable and therefore additional consideration may be required to address the gap with DORA as and when required.

source_description: Financial entities shall have in place internal governance and control frameworks that ensure an effective and prudent management of all ICT risks, in accordance with Article 6(4), in order to achieve a high level of digital operational resilience.
addendum:
Missing specification(s) in the CCM v4.1: 
"in accordance with Article 6(4)."
analysis:
5.1 is covered by the CCM controls mapped; however, it calls out article 6(4) where there is partial coverage, therefore the gap stated is also here.

Note that this provision explicitly references Chapters III, IV, and V, creating a cross-reference dependency. The gap description should perhaps note that CCM lacks a framework-wide proportionality mechanism that allows controls to scale based on entity size/complexity.

source_description: The management body of the financial entity shall define, approve, oversee and be responsible for the implementation of all arrangements related to the ICT risk management framework referred to in Article 6(1).
Management body shall bear the ultimate responsibility for managing the financial entity’s ICT risk;
Management body shall put in place policies that aim to ensure the maintenance of high standards of availability, authenticity, integrity and confidentiality, of data;

Management body shall set clear roles and responsibilities for all ICT-related functions and establish appropriate governance arrangements to ensure effective and timely communication, cooperation and coordination among those functions;
addendum:
Missing specification(s) in the CCM v4.1: 
"Establish appropriate governance arrangements to ensure effective and timely communication, cooperation and coordination among those functions."
analysis:
GRC-06 does not address the establishment of appropriate governance arrangements to ensure effective and timely communication, cooperation, and coordination among those functions.

DORA's requirement for "timely communication, cooperation and coordination among those functions" implies a specific SLA or timeliness expectation that is absent from GRC-06. This is operationally significant for financial entities.

source_description: Management body shall bear the overall responsibility for setting and approving the digital operational resilience strategy as referred to in Article 6(8), including the determination of the appropriate risk tolerance level of ICT risk of the financial entity, as referred to in Article 6(8), point (b);

Management body shall approve, oversee and periodically review the implementation of the financial entity's ICT business continuity policy and ICT response and recovery plans, referred to, respectively, in Article 11(1) and (3), which may be adopted as a dedicated specific policy forming an integral part of the financial entity's overall business continuity policy and response and recovery plan;
Management body shall approve and periodically review the financial entity's ICT internal audit plans, ICT audits and material modifications to them;

Management body shall allocate and periodically review the appropriate budget to fulfil the financial entity’s digital operational resilience needs in respect of all types of resources, including relevant ICT security awareness programmes and digital operational resilience training referred to in Article 13(6), and ICT skills for all staff;
addendum:
Missing specification(s) in the CCM v4.1: 
 "digital operational resilience training."
analysis:
Reference HRS-11 does not explicitly address aspects of Digital Resilience & ICT Skills training for all staff.

The gap regarding "digital operational resilience training" for "all staff" is correctly identified. Consider adding: "CCM's training controls are generally role-based, whereas DORA requires entity-wide coverage including non-technical staff awareness of digital resilience concepts."

source_description: Management body shall approve and periodically review the financial entity’s policy on arrangements regarding the use of ICT services provided by ICT third-party service providers;
Management body shall put in place, at corporate level, reporting channels enabling it to be duly informed of arrangements concluded with ICT third-party service providers on the use of ICT services.
addendum:
Missing specification(s) in the CCM v4.1: 
"put in place, at corporate level, reporting channels."
analysis:
There is no explicit reference in CCM about the establishment of reporting channels for upward reporting channels to management body to be informed of arrangements with third-party providers. While arrangements can be interpreted and incorporated into contractual agreements covered in STA-11 and STA-13, there is no explicit reporting reference, although it could be implied.

DORA mandates formal, documented reporting channels at a corporate level for third-party ICT arrangements, implying board-level visibility. CCM's STA controls focus on contractual and operational management rather than corporate governance reporting structures.

source_description: Management body shall put in place, at corporate level, reporting channels enabling it to be duly informed of any relevant planned material changes regarding the ICT third-party service providers.
addendum:
Missing specification(s) in the CCM v4.1: 
"put in place, at corporate level, reporting channels."
analysis: Planned material changes refers to significant upcoming alterations to arrangements with ICT third-party service providers that could affect the financial entity's risk profile, operational resilience, or continuity of critical functions, which CCC-05 covers sufficiently. Gap remains on the "reporting channels" that must be in place.

source_description: Management body shall put in place, at corporate level, reporting channels enabling it to be duly informed of the potential impact of such changes on the critical or important functions subject to those arrangements, including a risk analysis summary to assess the impact of those changes, and at least major ICT-related incidents and their impact, as well as response, recovery and corrective measures.
ccm_controls: CCC-03; STA-07; STA-09; STA-13; SEF-03; SEF-09
addendum:
Missing specification(s) in the CCM v4.1: 
"put in place, at corporate level, reporting channels."
analysis: CCM covers incident response but does not explicitly require corporate-level reporting channels that consolidate risk analysis with corrective measures for third-party changes.

source_description: Financial entities other than microenterprises shall establish a role to monitor the arrangements concluded with ICT third-party service providers on the use of ICT services, or shall designate a member of senior management as responsible for overseeing the related risk exposure and relevant documentation.

Members of the management body of the financial entity shall actively keep up to date with sufficient knowledge and skills to understand and assess ICT risk and its impact on the operations of the financial entity, including by following specific training on a regular basis, commensurate to the ICT risk being managed.

Financial entities shall have a sound, comprehensive and well-documented ICT risk management framework as part of their overall risk management system, which enables them to address ICT risk quickly, efficiently and comprehensively and to ensure a high level of digital operational resilience.

The ICT risk management framework shall include at least strategies, policies, procedures, ICT protocols and tools that are necessary to duly and adequately protect all information assets and ICT assets, including computer software, hardware, servers, as well as to protect all relevant physical components and infrastructures, such as premises, data centres and sensitive designated areas, to ensure that all information assets and ICT assets are adequately protected from risks including damage and unauthorised access or usage.
ccm_controls: GRC-01; GRC-02; GRC-05; DCS-01; DCS-08; DCS-10; DCS-11

source_description: In accordance with their ICT risk management framework, financial entities shall minimise the impact of ICT risk by deploying appropriate strategies, policies, procedures, ICT protocols and tools. They shall provide complete and updated information on ICT risk and on their ICT risk management framework to the competent authorities upon their request.
ccm_controls: GRC-01; GRC-02; GRC-05; BCR-03; SEF-07; SEF-08
addendum:
Missing specification(s) in the CCM v4.1: 
'They shall provide complete and updated information on ICT risk and on their ICT risk management framework to the competent authorities upon their request.'.
analysis: A minor gap exists primarily in the nature of providing all relevant information on the entire ICT risk management framework.

source_description: Financial entities, other than microenterprises, shall assign the responsibility for managing and overseeing ICT risk to a control function and ensure an appropriate level of independence of such control function in order to avoid conflicts of interest. Financial entities shall ensure appropriate segregation and independence of ICT risk management functions, control functions, and internal audit functions, according to the three lines of defence model, or an internal risk management and control model.
addendum:
Missing specification(s) in the CCM v4.1: 
"appropriate level of independence of such control function in order to avoid conflicts of interest" and
"according to the three lines of defence model."
analysis: DORA explicitly mandates the "three lines of defence model" by name, requiring segregation of: (1) ICT risk management functions, (2) control functions, and (3) internal audit functions. CCM addresses these as separate control domains but does not prescribe a specific organizational model or require independence between them. Financial entities should document their "three lines of defence" structure as a DORA-specific implementation.

source_description: The ICT risk management framework shall be documented and reviewed at least once a year, or periodically in the case of microenterprises, as well as upon the occurrence of major ICT-related incidents, and following supervisory instructions or conclusions derived from relevant digital operational resilience testing or audit processes. It shall be continuously improved on the basis of lessons derived from implementation and monitoring. A report on the review of the ICT risk management framework shall be submitted to the competent authority upon its request.

The ICT risk management framework of financial entities, other than microenterprises, shall be subject to internal audit by auditors on a regular basis in line with the financial entities’ audit plan. Those auditors shall possess sufficient knowledge, skills and expertise in ICT risk, as well as appropriate independence. The frequency and focus of ICT audits shall be commensurate to the ICT risk of the financial entity.
addendum:
Missing specification(s) in the CCM v4.1: 
"auditors shall possess sufficient knowledge, skills and expertise in ICT risk" and
"The frequency and focus of ICT audits shall be commensurate to the ICT risk of the financial entity."
analysis: DORA's requirement that "frequency and focus of ICT audits shall be commensurate to the ICT risk" implies a dynamic, risk-proportionate audit cadence. CCM's A&A controls establish audit processes but do not mandate this proportionality mechanism.

source_description: Based on the conclusions from the internal audit review, financial entities shall establish a formal follow-up process, including rules for the timely verification and remediation of critical ICT audit findings.
The ICT risk management framework shall include a digital operational resilience strategy setting out how the framework shall be implemented.

The digital operational resilience strategy shall include methods to address ICT risk and attain specific ICT objectives, by explaining how the ICT risk management framework supports the financial entity’s business strategy and objectives;

The digital operational resilience strategy shall include methods to address ICT risk and attain specific ICT objectives, by establishing the risk tolerance level for ICT risk, in accordance with the risk appetite of the financial entity, and analysing the impact tolerance for ICT disruptions;

The digital operational resilience strategy shall include methods to address ICT risk and attain specific ICT objectives, by setting out clear information security objectives, including key performance indicators and key risk metrics;
addendum:
Missing specification(s) in the CCM v4.1: 
"including key performance indicators and key risk metrics."
analysis: DORA requires "key performance indicators and key risk metrics" as mandatory components of the digital operational resilience strategy. CCM addresses metrics in various controls but does not mandate specific ICT resilience KPIs/KRIs at the strategy level.

source_description: The digital operational resilience strategy shall include methods to address ICT risk and attain specific ICT objectives, by explaining the ICT reference architecture and any changes needed to reach specific business objectives;
addendum:
Missing specification(s) in the CCM v4.1: 
"by explaining the ICT reference architecture."
analysis: An "ICT reference architecture" is a specific DORA requirement implying a documented, standardized view of the entity's technology landscape. This is an enterprise architecture artifact not explicitly required by CCM.

source_description: The digital operational resilience strategy shall include methods to address ICT risk and attain specific ICT objectives, by outlining the different mechanisms put in place to detect ICT-related incidents, prevent their impact and provide protection from it;
ccm_controls: GRC-02; BCR-02; BCR-03; SEF-02; SEF-06; SEF-07

source_description: The digital operational resilience strategy shall include methods to address ICT risk and attain specific ICT objectives, by evidencing the current digital operational resilience situation on the basis of the number of major ICT-related incidents reported and the effectiveness of preventive measures;

The digital operational resilience strategy shall include methods to address ICT risk and attain specific ICT objectives, by implementing digital operational resilience testing, in accordance with Chapter IV of this Regulation;

The digital operational resilience strategy shall include methods to address ICT risk and attain specific ICT objectives, by outlining a communication strategy in the event of ICT-related incidents the disclosure of which is required in accordance with Article 14.

Financial entities may, in the context of the digital operational resilience strategy referred to in paragraph 8, define a holistic ICT multi-vendor strategy, at group or entity level, showing key dependencies on ICT third-party service providers and explaining the rationale behind the procurement mix of ICT third-party service providers.
addendum:
Missing specification(s) in the CCM v4.1: 
"define a holistic ICT multi-vendor strategy, at group or entity level, showing key dependencies on ICT third-party service providers and explaining the rationale behind the procurement mix of ICT third-party service providers."
analysis: DORA requires a "holistic ICT multi-vendor strategy" that documents: (1) key dependencies on ICT third-party providers, (2) rationale behind the procurement mix, and (3) group/entity level view. This is a strategic vendor risk management requirement that goes significantly beyond CCM's STA controls, which focus on individual vendor management rather than portfolio-level strategy.

source_description: Financial entities may, in accordance with Union and national sectoral law, outsource the tasks of verifying compliance with ICT risk management requirements to intra-group or external undertakings. In case of such outsourcing, the financial entity remains fully responsible for the verification of compliance with the ICT risk management requirements.
addendum: Recommend that CCM uses the full DORA provision to close the gap. The mapped CCM controls cover in part the high specificity of the DORA provision objective.

source_description: In order to address and manage ICT risk, financial entities shall use and maintain updated ICT systems, protocols and tools that are appropriate to the magnitude of operations supporting the conduct of their activities, in accordance with the proportionality principle as referred to in Article 4;
addendum:
Missing specification(s) in the CCM v4.1: 
"in accordance with the proportionality principle."
analysis: GRC covers for ICT risk and CCC-04 as part of the change management process for updating assets, including systems protocols and tools. Similarly, TVM-05 and TVM-06 cover other applications and tools updates, including for third parties.

source_description: In order to address and manage ICT risk, financial entities shall use and maintain updated ICT systems, protocols and tools that are reliable;
ccm_controls: GRC-02; CCC-04; TVM-05; TVM-06; BCR-02; BCR-03

source_description: In order to address and manage ICT risk, financial entities shall use and maintain updated ICT systems, protocols and tools that are equipped with sufficient capacity to accurately process the data necessary for the performance of activities and the timely provision of services, and to deal with peak orders, message or transaction volumes, as needed, including where new technology is introduced;
ccm_controls: I&S-02; GRC-02; CCC-04; TVM-05; TVM-06; BCR-02; BCR-03

source_description: In order to address and manage ICT risk, financial entities shall use and maintain updated ICT systems, protocols and tools that are technologically resilient in order to adequately deal with additional information processing needs as required under stressed market conditions or other adverse situations.
ccm_controls: I&S-02; GRC-02; CCC-04; TVM-05; TVM-06; BCR-02; BCR-03

source_description: As part of the ICT risk management framework referred to in Article 6(1), financial entities shall identify, classify and adequately document all ICT supported business functions, roles and responsibilities, the information assets and ICT assets supporting those functions, and their roles and dependencies in relation to ICT risk. Financial entities shall review as needed, and at least yearly, the adequacy of this classification and of any relevant documentation.
ccm_controls: DCS-06; DCS-07; DSP-03; DSP-04; DSP-07; GRC-01; GRC-02; GRC-03; GRC-06; HRS-09; BCR-02

source_description: Financial entities shall, on a continuous basis, identify all sources of ICT risk, in particular the risk exposure to and from other financial entities, and assess cyber threats and ICT vulnerabilities relevant to their ICT supported business functions, information assets and ICT assets. Financial entities shall review on a regular basis, and at least yearly, the risk scenarios impacting them.
ccm_controls: GRC-02; TVM-01; TVM-02; TVM-03; TVM-04; TVM-10; TVM-11
addendum:
Missing specification(s) in the CCM v4.1: 
"identify the risk exposure to and from other financial entities" and
"financial entities shall review on a regular basis, and at least yearly, the risk scenarios impacting them."
analysis: DORA recognizes interconnectedness risk as a systemic concern unique to the financial sector. The requirement to identify risk exposure "to and from other financial entities" implies a network/ecosystem view of ICT risk that extends beyond the organization's perimeter. CCM's asset and risk identification controls are entity-centric and do not address this inter-institutional risk dimension. CCM covers general risk management, threat/vulnerability analysis, and reporting; however, it lacks explicit and continuous monitoring of ICT risk exposures between financial entities.

source_description: Financial entities, other than microenterprises, shall perform a risk assessment upon each major change in the network and information system infrastructure, in the processes or procedures affecting their ICT supported business functions, information assets or ICT assets.

Financial entities shall identify all information assets and ICT assets, including those on remote sites, network resources and hardware equipment, and shall map those considered critical. They shall map the configuration of the information assets and ICT assets and the links and interdependencies between the different information assets and ICT assets.
ccm_controls: CCC-01; CCC-06; DCS-07; UEM-04; UEM-14; DSP-05; I&S-08; I&S-09

source_description: Financial entities shall identify and document all processes that are dependent on ICT third-party service providers, and shall identify interconnections with ICT third-party service providers that provide services that support critical or important functions.
For the purposes of paragraphs 1, 4 and 5, financial entities shall maintain relevant inventories and update them periodically and every time any major change as referred to in paragraph 3 occurs.

Financial entities, other than microenterprises, shall on a regular basis, and at least yearly, conduct a specific ICT risk assessment on all legacy ICT systems and, in any case before and after connecting technologies, applications or systems.
addendum:
Missing specification(s) in the CCM v4.1: 
"conduct a specific ICT risk assessment on all legacy ICT systems and, in any case before and after connecting technologies, applications or systems."
analysis: DORA explicitly calls out "legacy ICT systems" as requiring specific, dedicated risk assessments. Additionally, assessments are required "before and after connecting technologies, applications or systems." CCM covers change management and risk assessment but does not: (1) define or specifically address legacy systems, (2) mandate pre- and post-connection assessments, or (3) require annual legacy-specific reviews. Financial entities should implement legacy system identification and assessment as a DORA-specific process.

source_description: For the purposes of adequately protecting ICT systems and with a view to organizing response measures, financial entities shall continuously monitor and control the security and functioning of ICT systems and tools and shall minimize the impact of ICT risk on ICT systems through the deployment of appropriate ICT security tools, policies and procedures.

Financial entities shall design, procure and implement ICT security policies, procedures, protocols and tools that aim to ensure the resilience, continuity and availability of ICT systems, in particular for those supporting critical or important functions, and to maintain high standards of availability, authenticity, integrity and confidentiality of data, whether at rest, in use or in transit.
In order to achieve the objectives referred to in paragraph 2, financial entities shall use ICT solutions and processes that are appropriate in accordance with Article 4.
The ICT solutions and processes shall ensure the security of the means of transfer of data;
The ICT solutions and processes shall minimize the risk of corruption or loss of data, unauthorized access and technical flaws that may hinder business activity;
The ICT solutions and processes shall prevent the lack of availability, the impairment of the authenticity and integrity, the breaches of confidentiality and the loss of data;
The ICT solutions and processes shall ensure that data is protected from risks arising from data management, including poor administration, processing-related risks and human error.

As part of the ICT risk management framework referred to in Article 6(1), financial entities shall develop and document an information security policy defining rules to protect the availability, authenticity, integrity and confidentiality of data, information assets and ICT assets, including those of their customers, where applicable;

As part of the ICT risk management framework referred to in Article 6(1), financial entities shall following a risk-based approach, establish a sound network and infrastructure management structure using appropriate techniques, methods and protocols that may include implementing automated mechanisms to isolate affected information assets in the event of cyber-attacks;

For the purposes of the first subparagraph, point (b), financial entities shall design the network connection infrastructure in a way that allows it to be instantaneously severed or segmented in order to minimize and prevent contagion, especially for interconnected financial processes.

As part of the ICT risk management framework referred to in Article 6(1), financial entities shall implement policies that limit the physical or logical access to information assets and ICT assets to what is required for legitimate and approved functions and activities only, and establish to that end a set of policies, procedures and controls that address access rights and ensure a sound administration thereof;

As part of the ICT risk management framework referred to in Article 6(1), financial entities shall implement policies and protocols for strong authentication mechanisms, based on relevant standards and dedicated control systems, and protection measures of cryptographic keys whereby data is encrypted based on results of approved data classification and ICT risk assessment processes;

As part of the ICT risk management framework referred to in Article 6(1), financial entities shall implement documented policies, procedures and controls for ICT change management, including changes to software, hardware, firmware components, systems or security parameters, that are based on a risk assessment approach and are an integral part of the financial entity’s overall change management process, in order to ensure that all changes to ICT systems are recorded, tested, assessed, approved, implemented and verified in a controlled manner;

For the purposes of the first subparagraph, point (e), the ICT change management process shall be approved by appropriate lines of management and shall have specific protocols in place.
ccm_controls: CCC-01; CCC-02; CCC-03; CCC-04; CCC-05; CEK-05; CEK-06

source_description: As part of the ICT risk management framework referred to in Article 6(1), financial entities shall have appropriate and comprehensive documented policies for patches and updates.

Financial entities shall have in place mechanisms to promptly detect anomalous activities, in accordance with Article 17, including ICT network performance issues and ICT-related incidents, and to identify potential material single points of failure.
All detection mechanisms referred to in the first subparagraph shall be regularly tested in accordance with Article 25.
addendum:
Missing specification(s) in the CCM v4.1: 
"identify potential material single points of failure."
analysis: DORA's requirement to "identify potential material single points of failure" implies network topology analysis and dependency mapping specifically for SPOF identification. CCM's monitoring controls address anomaly detection but do not mandate SPOF analysis as a specific detection activity.

source_description: The detection mechanisms referred to in paragraph 1 shall enable multiple layers of control, define alert thresholds and criteria to trigger and initiate ICT-related incident response processes, including automatic alert mechanisms for relevant staff in charge of ICT-related incident response.
ccm_controls: LOG-01; LOG-03; LOG-05; I&S-09; SEF-07; SEF-03

source_description: Financial entities shall devote sufficient resources and capabilities to monitor user activity, the occurrence of ICT anomalies and ICT-related incidents, in particular cyber-attacks.
ccm_controls: LOG-05; IAM-03; SEF-02; SEF-05; SEF-07; TVM-02; I&S-03

source_description: Data reporting service providers shall, in addition, have in place systems that can effectively check trade reports for completeness, identify omissions and obvious errors, and request re-transmission of those reports.
addendum: The full DORA provision is missing from CCM v4.1 and has to be used to close the gap.
analysis: This provision is specific to "data reporting service providers," a DORA-defined category of financial market infrastructure. The requirements for trade report verification, completeness checks, and re-transmission requests are sector-specific and outside CCM's scope. Entities classified as data reporting service providers should implement this as a regulatory-specific control.

source_description: As part of the ICT risk management framework referred to in Article 6(1) and based on the identification requirements set out in Article 8, financial entities shall put in place a comprehensive ICT business continuity policy, which may be adopted as a dedicated specific policy, forming an integral part of the overall business continuity policy of the financial entity.

Financial entities shall implement the ICT business continuity policy through dedicated, appropriate and documented arrangements, plans, procedures and mechanisms aiming to ensure the continuity of the financial entity’s critical or important functions;

Financial entities shall implement the ICT business continuity policy through dedicated, appropriate and documented arrangements, plans, procedures and mechanisms aiming to quickly, appropriately and effectively respond to, and resolve, all ICT-related incidents in a way that limits damage and prioritizes the resumption of activities and recovery actions;

Financial entities shall implement the ICT business continuity policy through dedicated, appropriate and documented arrangements, plans, procedures and mechanisms aiming to activate, without delay, dedicated plans that enable containment measures, processes and technologies suited to each type of ICT-related incident and prevent further damage, as well as tailored response and recovery procedures established in accordance with Article 12;

Financial entities shall implement the ICT business continuity policy through dedicated, appropriate and documented arrangements, plans, procedures and mechanisms aiming to estimate preliminary impacts, damages and losses;

Financial entities shall implement the ICT business continuity policy through dedicated, appropriate and documented arrangements, plans, procedures and mechanisms aiming to set out communication and crisis management actions that ensure that updated information is transmitted to all relevant internal staff and external stakeholders in accordance with Article 14, and report to the competent authorities in accordance with Article 19.
ccm_controls: BCR-01; BCR-04; SEF-01; SEF-02; SEF-03; SEF-07

source_description: As part of the ICT risk management framework referred to in Article 6(1), financial entities shall implement associated ICT response and recovery plans which, in the case of financial entities other than microenterprises, shall be subject to independent internal audit reviews.

Financial entities shall put in place, maintain and periodically test appropriate ICT business continuity plans, notably with regard to critical or important functions outsourced or contracted through arrangements with ICT third-party service providers.

As part of the overall business continuity policy, financial entities shall conduct a business impact analysis (BIA) of their exposures to severe business disruptions. Under the BIA, financial entities shall assess the potential impact of severe business disruptions by means of quantitative and qualitative criteria, using internal and external data and scenario analysis, as appropriate. The BIA shall consider the criticality of identified and mapped business functions, support processes, third-party dependencies and information assets, and their interdependencies. Financial entities shall ensure that ICT assets and ICT services are designed and used in full alignment with the BIA, in particular with regard to adequately ensuring the redundancy of all critical components.
ccm_controls: BCR-01; BCR-02; BCR-03; BCR-05; STA-08; BCR-11

source_description:
As part of their comprehensive ICT risk management, financial entities shall test the crisis communication plans established in accordance with Article 14.    

Financial entities shall regularly review their  ICT response and recovery plans, taking into account the results of tests carried out in accordance with the first subparagraph and recommendations stemming from audit checks or supervisory reviews.
ccm_controls: GRC-02; A&A-06; BCR-07; BCR-10; SEF-03; SEF-04; SEF-09

source_description: Financial entities, other than microenterprises, shall have a crisis management function, which, in the event of activation of their ICT business continuity plans or ICT response and recovery plans, shall, set out clear procedures to manage internal and external crisis communications in accordance with Article 14.
Financial entities shall keep readily accessible records of activities before and during disruption events when their ICT business continuity plans and ICT response and recovery plans are activated.
addendum:
Missing specification(s) in the CCM v4.1: 
"shall keep readily accessible records of activities before and during disruption events."
analysis: The CCM controls cover logging and recording activities comprehensively. However, DORA's specific emphasis is on keeping these records "readily accessible" and explicitly links this requirement to the activation of ICT business continuity plans and ICT response and recovery plans, for activities "before and during disruption events." While CCM enables this, DORA makes it a specific, mandatory outcome tied to the activation of these plans. This implies pre-positioned or replicated records specifically designed for disruption scenarios, not just general logging. The records must be accessible even when primary systems are unavailable, implying architectural considerations beyond standard logging controls.

source_description: Central securities depositories shall provide the competent authorities with copies of the results of the ICT business continuity tests, or of similar exercises.
addendum: Recommend that CCM uses the full DORA provision to close the gap. The mapped CCM controls cover in part the high specificity of the DORA provision objective.
analysis: This is a sector-specific reporting requirement for CSDs. CCM controls address testing but do not address regulatory reporting of test results. CSDs should implement this as a compliance process.

source_description: Financial entities, other than microenterprises, shall report to the competent authorities, upon their request, an estimation of aggregated annual costs and losses caused by major ICT-related incidents.
addendum: Recommend that CCM uses the full DORA provision to close the gap. The mapped CCM controls cover in part the high specificity of the DORA provision objective.
analysis:
While CCM enables the collection of data that could contribute to estimating costs and losses (SEF-01 for impact, GRC-02 for risk) and has a general metric control (SEF-05), it does not explicitly mandate the estimation of aggregated annual costs and losses caused by major ICT-related incidents as a specific output, nor does it specify this as a report to competent authorities upon request for non-microenterprises. This is a direct, granular reporting requirement in DORA not fully captured in CCM.

This is a specific regulatory reporting requirement for "aggregated annual costs and losses caused by major ICT-related incidents." This implies: (1) a cost tracking/attribution methodology, (2) incident classification as "major," and (3) annual aggregation for regulatory submission. None of these are CCM requirements.

source_description: For the purpose of ensuring the restoration of ICT systems and data with minimum downtime, limited disruption and loss, as part of their ICT risk management framework, financial entities shall develop and document backup policies and procedures specifying the scope of the data that is subject to the backup and the minimum frequency of the backup, based on the criticality of information or the confidentiality level of the data;
addendum:
Missing specification(s) in the CCM v4.1: 
"specifying the scope of the data that is subject to the backup and the minimum frequency of the backup, based on the criticality of information or the confidentiality level of the data."
analysis: DORA explicitly links backup scope and frequency to "criticality of information" and "confidentiality level of the data." This implies a data classification-driven backup policy, which CCM addresses generically but does not prescribe with this level of data-attribute specificity.

source_description: For the purpose of ensuring the restoration of ICT systems and data with minimum downtime, limited disruption and loss, as part of their ICT risk management framework, financial entities shall develop and document restoration and recovery procedures and methods.

Financial entities shall set up backup systems that can be activated in accordance with the backup policies and procedures, as well as restoration and recovery procedures and methods. The activation of backup systems shall not jeopardise the security of the network and information systems or the availability, authenticity, integrity or confidentiality of data. Testing of the backup procedures and restoration and recovery procedures and methods shall be undertaken periodically.
addendum:
Missing specification(s) in the CCM v4.1: 
"activated in accordance with the backup policies and procedures, as well as restoration and recovery procedures and methods."
analysis: CCM introduces no requirements on back-up policies and procedures or restoration and recovery procedures and methods. Although they might be implied under BCR-01, they are not stated explicitly.

source_description:
When restoring backup data using own systems, financial entities shall use ICT systems that are physically and logically segregated from the source ICT system. The ICT systems shall be securely protected from any unauthorized access or ICT corruption and allow for the timely restoration of services making use of data and system backups as necessary.

For central counterparties, the recovery plans shall enable the recovery of all transactions at the time of disruption to allow the central counterparty to continue to operate with certainty and to complete settlement on the scheduled date.

Data reporting service providers shall additionally maintain adequate resources and have back-up and restoration facilities in place in order to offer and maintain their services at all times.
ccm_controls: BCR-08; BCR-09; BCR-11; IAM-06; IAM-08; CEK-03; I&S-02
addendum:
Missing specification(s) in the CCM v4.1: 
"For central counterparties (CCP), the recovery plans shall enable the recovery of all transactions at the time of disruption to allow the central counterparty to continue to operate with certainty and to complete settlement on the scheduled date."
analysis: The central counterparties (CCP)-specific requirement for "recovery of all transactions at the time of disruption" with "certainty" and "scheduled date settlement" is a financial market infrastructure requirement with zero-data-loss implications. This is significantly more stringent than generic BCR controls and should be implemented as a sector-specific control for CCPs.

source_description: Financial entities, other than microenterprises, shall maintain redundant ICT capacities equipped with resources, capabilities and functions that are adequate to ensure business needs. Microenterprises shall assess the need to maintain such redundant ICT capacities based on their risk profile.
Central securities depositories shall maintain at least one secondary processing site endowed with adequate resources, capabilities, functions and staffing arrangements to ensure business needs.

The secondary processing site shall be located at a geographical distance from the primary processing site to ensure that it bears a distinct risk profile and to prevent it from being affected by the event which has affected the primary site;

The secondary processing site shall be capable of ensuring the continuity of critical or important functions identically to the primary site, or providing the level of services necessary to ensure that the financial entity performs its critical operations within the recovery objectives;

The secondary processing site shall be immediately accessible to the financial entity’s staff to ensure continuity of critical or important functions in the event that the primary processing site has become unavailable.
addendum:
Missing specification(s) in the CCM v4.1: 
"The secondary processing site shall be immediately accessible to the financial entity’s staff."

source_description: In determining the recovery time and recovery point objectives for each function, financial entities shall take into account whether it is a critical or important function and the potential overall impact on market efficiency. Such time objectives shall ensure that, in extreme scenarios, the agreed service levels are met.

When recovering from an ICT-related incident, financial entities shall perform necessary checks, including any multiple checks and reconciliations, in order to ensure that the highest level of data integrity is maintained. These checks shall also be performed when reconstructing data from external stakeholders, in order to ensure that all data is consistent between systems.
addendum:
Missing specification(s) in the CCM v4.1: 
"checks shall also be performed when reconstructing data from external stakeholders, in order to ensure that all data is consistent between systems."
analysis: While CCM enables organizations to define, implement, and evaluate processes, procedures, and technical measures for timely and effective response to security incidents, in accordance with incident categories and severity levels, and to review, update, and test processes and procedures at least annually, it does not specifically mention performing necessary checks, including any multiple checks and reconciliations, in order to ensure that the highest level of data integrity is maintained. These checks shall also be performed when reconstructing data from external stakeholders, in order to ensure that all data is consistent between systems.

source_description: Financial entities shall have in place capabilities and staff to gather information on vulnerabilities and cyber threats, ICT-related incidents, in particular cyber-attacks, and analyse the impact they are likely to have on their digital operational resilience.
ccm_controls: SEF-03; SEF-06; SEF-09; SEF-10; TVM-03; TVM-04; BCR-02

source_description:
Financial entities shall put in place post ICT-related incident reviews after a major ICT-related incident disrupts their core activities, analysing the causes of disruption and identifying required improvements to the ICT operations or within the ICT business continuity policy referred to in Article 11.
Financial entities, other than microenterprises, shall, upon request, communicate to the competent authorities, the changes that were implemented following post ICT-related incident reviews as referred to in the first subparagraph.
analysis:
SEF-09 covers for post-incident reviews and analysis, identifying the causes, and applying correction measures. Covers first sentence of the DORA provision.
BCR-01 refers to BC and OR policy, procedures, and evaluation.
SEF-03 covers for the communication aspect of incident-related information as part of an incident management and response plan.

source_description: The post ICT-related incident reviews referred to in the first subparagraph shall determine whether the established procedures were followed and the actions taken were effective, including in relation to the promptness in responding to security alerts and determining the impact of ICT-related incidents and their severity;
analysis: SEF-07 covers for the promptness in responding to security alerts and determining the impact of security incidents and severity, while SEF-09 is a post-incident review control that determines whether SEF-07 was effective.

source_description: The post ICT-related incident reviews referred to in the first subparagraph shall determine whether the established procedures were followed and the actions taken were effective, including in relation to the quality and speed of performing a forensic analysis, where deemed appropriate;
addendum:
Missing specification(s) in the CCM v4.1: 
"the quality and speed of performing a forensic analysis, where deemed appropriate."
analysis: DORA is more direct in this regard. Companies can consider expressly requiring an assessment of whether processes were followed as appropriate. This is not expressly mandated under CCM. The speed of forensic analysis is also specified in DORA but not CCM. This can be added as an assessment to meet the DORA requirement.

source_description: The post ICT-related incident reviews referred to in the first subparagraph shall determine whether the established procedures were followed and the actions taken were effective, including in relation to the effectiveness of incident escalation within the financial entity;
addendum:
Missing specification(s) in the CCM v4.1: 
"the effectiveness of incident escalation within the financial entity."

source_description: The post ICT-related incident reviews referred to in the first subparagraph shall determine whether the established procedures were followed and the actions taken were effective, including in relation to the effectiveness of internal and external communication.
analysis: SEF-03 covers for stakeholder communication (both internal and external) about incident-related information.

source_description: Lessons derived from the digital operational resilience testing carried out in accordance with Articles 26 and 27 and from real life ICT-related incidents, in particular cyber-attacks, along with challenges faced upon the activation of ICT business continuity plans and ICT response and recovery plans, together with relevant information exchanged with counterparts and assessed during supervisory reviews, shall be duly incorporated on a continuous basis into the ICT risk assessment process. Those findings shall form the basis for appropriate reviews of relevant components of the ICT risk management framework referred to in Article 6(1).
ccm_controls: BCR-04; BCR-06; BCR-10; SEF-04; SEF-04; SEF-09
addendum: Recommend that CCM uses the full DORA provision to close the gap. The mapped CCM controls cover in part the high specificity of the DORA provision objective.
analysis:
As DORA is more direct and detailed than CCM in this regard, companies can consider adding the following to ongoing IT risk processes: specific checks for and/or specific requirements for incorporating lessons and findings from DORT, BC/OR response challenges, industry information sharing, and outputs from regulator reviews.

DORA is more direct and detailed than CCM.

source_description: Financial entities shall monitor the effectiveness of the implementation of their digital operational resilience strategy set out in Article 6(8). They shall map the evolution of ICT risk over time, analyse the frequency, types, magnitude and evolution of ICT-related incidents, in particular cyber-attacks and their patterns, with a view to understanding the level of ICT risk exposure, in particular in relation to critical or important functions, and enhance the cyber maturity and preparedness of the financial entity.
addendum:
Missing specification(s) in the CCM v4.1: 
"monitor the effectiveness of the implementation of their digital operational resilience strategy" and
"shall map the evolution of ICT risk over time, analyse the frequency, types, magnitude and evolution of ICT-related incidents, in particular cyber-attacks and their patterns."
analysis: DORA requires specific monitoring of: (1) effectiveness of digital operational resilience strategy implementation, (2) evolution of ICT risk over time, (3) frequency, types, magnitude, and evolution of ICT-related incidents, and (4) patterns of cyberattacks. This creates a formal resilience metrics program that is more prescriptive than CCM's general monitoring controls.

source_description: Senior ICT staff shall report at least yearly to the management body on the findings referred to in paragraph 3 and put forward recommendations.

Financial entities shall develop ICT security awareness programmes and digital operational resilience training as compulsory modules in their staff training schemes. Those programmes and training shall be applicable to all employees and to senior management staff, and shall have a level of complexity commensurate to the remit of their functions. Where appropriate, financial entities shall also include ICT third-party service providers in their relevant training schemes in accordance with Article 30(2), point (i).
addendum:
Missing specification(s) in the CCM v4.1: 
"Financial entities shall develop...digital operational resilience training as compulsory modules in their staff training schemes" and "shall also include ICT third-party service providers in their relevant training schemes."

source_description: Financial entities, other than microenterprises, shall monitor relevant technological developments on a continuous basis, also with a view to understanding the possible impact of the deployment of such new technologies on ICT security requirements and digital operational resilience. They shall keep up-to-date with the latest ICT risk management processes, in order to effectively combat current or new forms of cyber-attacks.
ccm_controls: TVM-01; TVM-03; TVM-04; BCR-01; GRC-02; GRC-03

source_description: As part of the ICT risk management framework referred to in Article 6(1), financial entities shall have in place crisis communication plans enabling a responsible disclosure of, at least, major ICT-related incidents or vulnerabilities to clients and counterparts as well as to the public, as appropriate.

As part of the ICT risk management framework, financial entities shall implement communication policies for internal staff and for external stakeholders. Communication policies for staff shall take into account the need to differentiate between staff involved in ICT risk management, in particular the staff responsible for response and recovery, and staff that needs to be informed.
At least one person in the financial entity shall be tasked with implementing the communication strategy for ICT-related incidents and fulfil the public and media function for that purpose.
addendum:
Missing specification(s) in the CCM v4.1: 
"fulfil the public and media function for that purpose."
analysis: While CCM enables a communication strategy for notifying relevant internal departments, impacted service customers, and other business critical relationships that may be impacted (such as supply chain), it does not mandate that at least one person in the financial entity shall be tasked with implementing the communication strategy for ICT-related incidents and fulfill the public and media function for that purpose.

source_description: Articles 5 to 15 of this Regulation shall not apply to small and non-interconnected investment firms, payment institutions exempted pursuant to Directive (EU) 2015/2366; institutions exempted pursuant to Directive 2013/36/EU in respect of which Member States have decided not to apply the option referred to in Article 2(4) of this Regulation; electronic money institutions exempted pursuant to Directive 2009/110/EC; and small institutions for occupational retirement provision.
addendum: DORA provision out of scope of cybersecurity.
analysis: DORA provision out of scope of cybersecurity.

source_description: Without prejudice to the first subparagraph, the entities listed in the first subparagraph shall put in place and maintain a sound and documented ICT risk management framework that details the mechanisms and measures aimed at a quick, efficient and comprehensive management of ICT risk, including for the protection of relevant physical components and infrastructures;
analysis:
GRC-02 covers formal risk management.
DSP-01 covers having policies and procedures in place.
DCS-08 covers the protection of physical infrastructure.
TVM-01 and LOG-03 cover detection, alerting, and response.

source_description: Without prejudice to the first subparagraph, the entities listed in the first subparagraph shall continuously monitor the security and functioning of all ICT systems;
analysis:
LOG-03 covers providing security monitoring and alerting.
LOG-05 covers audit logs monitoring and response.
IVS-03 covers network security to monitor the network traffic and configurations RBAC, netflows, and so on.

source_description: Without prejudice to the first subparagraph, the entities listed in the first subparagraph shall minimize the impact of ICT risk through the use of sound, resilient and updated ICT systems, protocols and tools which are appropriate to support the performance of their activities and the provision of services and adequately protect availability, authenticity, integrity and confidentiality of data in the network and information systems;
analysis:
A&A-01 covers sound selection. 
IVS-03 and IVS-04 cover resilience.
CCC-07 and UEM-05 cover continuous updating.
CEK-04 covers ensuring robust data protection via encryption.
LOG-07 covers ensuring that there is detection and validation in the ICT environment.

source_description: Without prejudice to the first subparagraph, the entities listed in the first subparagraph shall allow sources of ICT risk and anomalies in the network and information systems to be promptly identified and detected and ICT-related incidents to be swiftly handled;
analysis:
LOG-05 aims at the detection of anomalies, while LOG-03 covers implementing an alerting system.
SEF-03 covers documentation and procedures, along with playbooks for incident handling.
SEF-07 covers the technicalities and steps for swift incident handling and response.

source_description: Without prejudice to the first subparagraph, the entities listed in the first subparagraph shall identify key dependencies on ICT third-party service providers;
analysis:
STA-08 covers the development and maintenance of an inventory of all supply chain relationships.
STA-09 covers management of software bill of materials (SBOM) with review annually.
STA-11 covers the contractual agreement.

source_description: Without prejudice to the first subparagraph, the entities listed in the first subparagraph shall ensure the continuity of critical or important functions, through business continuity plans and response and recovery measures, which include, at least, back-up and restoration measures;
analysis:
BCR-02 is a control that is used to determine the criticality of business functions and adapt the BC and OR functions. 
BRC-03 jointly with BCR-04 aim at implementing response and recovery measures.
BCR-04 includes business continuity management planning.
BCR-08 covers the data backup and restoration.

source_description: Without prejudice to the first subparagraph, the entities listed in the first subparagraph shall test, on a regular basis, the plans and measures referred to in point (f), as well as the effectiveness of the controls implemented in accordance with points (a) and (c);
analysis:
BCR-06 and BCR-10 cover the BCP and digital risk protection testing.
The effectiveness of controls implementation takes place by both internal assessments and third-party audits covered within the A&A domain of the CCM, in particular A&A-02 and A&A-03.

source_description: Without prejudice to the first subparagraph, the entities listed in the first subparagraph shall implement, as appropriate, relevant operational conclusions resulting from the tests referred to in point (g) and from post-incident analysis into the ICT risk assessment process and develop, according to needs and ICT risk profile, ICT security awareness programmes and digital operational resilience training for staff and management.
addendum:
Missing specification(s) in the CCM v4.1:  
"implement, as appropriate, relevant operational conclusions resulting from the tests" and "digital operational resilience training for staff and management."

source_description: The ICT risk management framework referred to in paragraph 1, second subparagraph, point (a), shall be documented and reviewed periodically and upon the occurrence of major ICT-related incidents in compliance with supervisory instructions. It shall be continuously improved on the basis of lessons derived from implementation and monitoring. A report on the review of the ICT risk management framework shall be submitted to the competent authority upon its request.
addendum:
Missing specification(s) in the CCM v4.1:  
"The ICT risk management framework...shall be documented and reviewed periodically and upon the occurrence of major ICT-related incidents in compliance with supervisory instructions" and "a report on the review of the ICT risk management framework shall be submitted to the competent authority upon its request."

source_description: Financial entities shall define, establish and implement an ICT-related incident management process to detect, manage and notify ICT-related incidents.
ccm_controls: AIS-05; LOG-05; SEF-03; SEF-06; SEF-07; SEF-08
analysis:
AIS-05 and LOG-05 cover an automated, timely, and effective detection.
AIS-05 states, "Implement a testing strategy, including criteria for acceptance of new information systems, upgrades and new versions, which provides application security assurance and maintains compliance while meeting organizational delivery goals. Automate when applicable and possible."

LOG-05 states, "Implement and maintain capabilities to correlate and monitor security audit logs for the detection of suspicious or anomalous activity that deviates from typical or expected patterns. Establish and follow a defined process to review and take appropriate and timely actions on detected anomalies." 

SEF-03, SEF-06, SEF-07, and SEF-08 cover the requirement of implementing an incident management procedure. SEF-06 covers for "detect ICT-related incidents," as triaging involves evaluating a detected security event to determine whether it qualifies as a security incident. SEF-07 calls out a "process" and covers for the "incident management" and response.
SEF-03 states, "Establish, document, approve, communicate, apply, evaluate, and maintain a security incident response plan, which includes but is not limited to: a communication strategy." 
SEF-06 states, "Define, implement, and evaluate processes, procedures, and technical measures supporting business processes to triage security-related events."
SEF-07 states, "Define, implement, and evaluate processes, procedures, and technical measures for timely and effective response to security incidents in accordance with incident categories and severity levels. Review, update, and test processes and procedures at least annually."
SEF-08 states, "Define and implement processes, procedures, and technical measures for security breach notifications. Report material security breaches including any relevant supply chain breaches, as per applicable SLAs, laws, and regulations."

DORA definition of ICT-related incidents: "ICT-related incident" means a single event or a series of linked events unplanned by the financial entity that compromises the security of the network and information systems, and has an adverse impact on the availability, authenticity, integrity, or confidentiality of data, or on the services provided by the financial entity." The DORA definition comprises all the ICT incidents, as well as the security incidents.

Security Incident Management in the CCM covers all the aspects. Note that usually security incidents are considered a subset of the ICT-related incidents in the financial entities. It is suggested to evaluate if the Security Incident Management domain in CCM should be renamed simply Incident Management.

source_description: Financial entities shall record all ICT-related incidents and significant cyber threats. Financial entities shall establish appropriate procedures and processes to ensure a consistent and integrated monitoring, handling and follow-up of ICT-related incidents, to ensure that root causes are identified, documented and addressed in order to prevent the occurrence of such incidents.
analysis:
LOG-09 states, "Generate audit records containing relevant security information," which covers the monitoring capability.

TVM-04 states, "Define, implement, and evaluate a threat analysis process and procedures to identify, assess, and review the threat landscape for cloud systems. Build threat models according to industry best practices to inform the risk mitigation strategy."

SEF-09 states, "Establish and maintain a secure repository of security incident records. Regularly review the incident records to identify patterns, root causes, and systemic vulnerabilities, and implement relevant corrective measures." 

Both TVM-4 and SEF-09 cover the requirement of recording ICT incidents and root cause analysis.

source_description: The ICT-related incident management process referred to in paragraph 1 shall put in place early warning indicators;
analysis:
LOG-05 states, "Implement and maintain capabilities to correlate and monitor security audit logs for the detection of suspicious or anomalous activity that deviates from typical or expected patterns. Establish and follow a defined process to review and take appropriate and timely actions on detected anomalies," which covers an automated, timely, and effective detection.

SEF-03 states, "Establish, document, approve, communicate, apply, evaluate, and maintain a security incident response plan, which includes but is not limited to: a communication strategy."

SEF-06 states, "Define, implement, and evaluate processes, procedures, and technical measures supporting business processes to triage security-related events."

source_description: The ICT-related incident management process referred to in paragraph 1 shall establish procedures to identify, track, log, categorise and classify ICT-related incidents according to their priority and severity and according to the criticality of the services impacted, in accordance with the criteria set out in Article 18(1);
analysis:
LOG-03 states, "Identify and monitor security-related events within applications and the underlying infrastructure. Define and implement a system to generate alerts to responsible stakeholders based on such events and corresponding metrics."

LOG-07 states, "Establish, document, and implement which information meta/data system events should be logged. Review and update the scope at least annually or whenever there is a change in the threat environment."

SEF-09 states, "Establish and maintain a secure repository of security incident records. Regularly review the incident records to identify patterns, root causes, and systemic vulnerabilities, and implement relevant corrective measures."

source_description: The ICT-related incident management process referred to in paragraph 1 shall assign roles and responsibilities that need to be activated for different ICT-related incident types and scenarios;
addendum:
Missing specification(s) in the CCM v4.1: 
"roles and responsibilities that need to be activated for different ICT-related incident types and scenarios."
analysis:
GRC-06 states, "Define and document roles and responsibilities for planning, implementing, operating, assessing, and improving governance programs."

HRS-09 states, "The organization includes within the employment agreements provisions and/or terms for adherence to established information governance and security policies."

Partial gap due to its high specificity of a requirement to assign roles and responsibilities for incident management.

source_description: The ICT-related incident management process referred to in paragraph 1 shall set out plans for communication to staff, external stakeholders and media in accordance with Article 14 and for notification to clients, for internal escalation procedures, including ICT-related customer complaints, as well as for the provision of information to financial entities that act as counterparts, as appropriate;
analysis:
SEF-03 states, "Establish, document, approve, communicate, apply, evaluate, and maintain a security incident response plan, which includes but is not limited to: a communication strategy."

SEF-10 states, "Maintain points of contact for applicable regulation authorities, national and local law enforcement, and other legal jurisdictional authorities. Review and update the points of contact at least annually."

source_description: The ICT-related incident management process referred to in paragraph 1 shall ensure that at least major ICT-related incidents are reported to relevant senior management and inform the management body of at least major ICT-related incidents, explaining the impact, response and additional controls to be established as a result of such ICT-related incidents;
analysis:
SEF-03 states, "Establish, document, approve, communicate, apply, evaluate, and maintain a security incident response plan, which includes but is not limited to: a communication strategy"

SEF-06 states, "Define, implement, and evaluate processes, procedures, and technical measures supporting business processes to triage security-related events."

SEF-07 states, "Define, implement, and evaluate processes, procedures, and technical measures for timely and effective response to security incidents in accordance with incident categories and severity levels. Review, update, and test processes and procedures at least annually."

SEF-08 states, "Define and implement processes, procedures, and technical measures for security breach notifications. Report material security breaches including any relevant supply chain breaches, as per applicable SLAs, laws, and regulations."

source_description: The ICT-related incident management process referred to in paragraph 1 shall establish ICT-related incident response procedures to mitigate impacts and ensure that services become operational and secure in a timely manner.
analysis:
SEF-07 states, "Define, implement, and evaluate processes, procedures, and technical measures for timely and effective response to security incidents in accordance with incident categories and severity levels. Review, update, and test processes and procedures at least annually."

SEF-09 states, "Establish and maintain a secure repository of security incident records. Regularly review the incident records to identify patterns, root causes, and systemic vulnerabilities, and implement relevant corrective measures."

source_description: Financial entities shall classify ICT-related incidents and shall determine their impact based on the number and/or relevance of clients or financial counterparts affected and, where applicable, the amount or number of transactions affected by the ICT-related incident, and whether the ICT-related incident has caused reputational impact;
addendum:
Missing specification(s) in the CCM v4.1: 
"determine their impact based on the number and/or relevance of clients or financial counterparts affected" and
"the amount or number of transactions affected by the ICT-related incident, and whether the ICT-related incident has caused reputational impact."
analysis: The CCM framework lacks explicit and prescriptive criteria for classifying incidents based on the number or relevance of clients, the amount/number of transactions affected, or a direct assessment of reputational impact as mandatory classification metrics for the incident itself.

source_description: Financial entities shall classify ICT-related incidents and shall determine their impact based on the duration of the ICT-related incident, including the service downtime;
addendum:
Missing specification(s) in the CCM v4.1: 
"determine their impact based on the duration of the ICT-related incident, including the service downtime."
analysis: While CCM enables the measurement of temporal metrics, DORA explicitly requires these as direct classification criteria for the incident. CCM doesn't explicitly mandate that incidents must be classified based on these temporal metrics.

source_description: Financial entities shall classify ICT-related incidents and shall determine their impact based on the geographical spread with regard to the areas affected by the ICT-related incident, particularly if it affects more than two Member States;
addendum:
Missing specification(s) in the CCM v4.1: 
"shall determine their impact based on the geographical spread with regard to the areas affected by the ICT-related incident, particularly if it affects more than two Member States."
analysis: While CCM enables geographical tracking, it does not explicitly mandate classifying incidents based on their geographical spread, nor does it specify the particular DORA threshold of "more than two Member States."

source_description: Financial entities shall classify ICT-related incidents and shall determine their impact based on the data losses that the ICT-related incident entails, in relation to availability, authenticity, integrity or confidentiality of data;
ccm_controls: BCR-02; BCR-03; SEF-02; SEF-06; SEF-07; SEF-08
addendum:
Missing specification(s) in the CCM v4.1: 
"determine their impact based on the data losses that the ICT-related incident entails, in relation to availability, authenticity, integrity or confidentiality of data."
analysis: While CCM addresses data protection and general data-related impact, DORA specifically requires classifying incidents based on "data losses...in relation to availability, authenticity, integrity or confidentiality." The CCM does not explicitly mandate this as a direct, standalone incident classification criterion at this level of prescriptiveness.

source_description: Financial entities shall classify ICT-related incidents and shall determine their impact based on the criticality of the services affected, including the financial entity’s transactions and operations;
ccm_controls: BCR-02; BCR-03; SEF-02; SEF-06; SEF-07; SEF-08
addendum:
Missing specification(s) in the CCM v4.1: 
"including the financial entity’s transactions and operations."
analysis: While CCM broadly addresses service importance (e.g., business impact assessment, functional impact), DORA explicitly requires "transactions and operations" as a primary incident classification criterion.

source_description: Financial entities shall classify ICT-related incidents and shall determine their impact based on the economic impact, in particular direct and indirect costs and losses, of the ICT-related incident in both absolute and relative terms.
ccm_controls: BCR-02; BCR-03; SEF-02; SEF-06; SEF-07; SEF-08
addendum:
Missing specification(s) in the CCM v4.1: 
"economic impact, in particular direct and indirect costs and losses, of the ICT-related incident in both absolute and relative terms."
analysis: While CCM controls address financial impact generally as part of risk or asset valuation, DORA specifically mandates incident classification based on "economic impact," distinguishing between "direct and indirect costs and losses," and requiring assessment in "absolute and relative terms." CCM lacks this prescriptive detail for incident classification.

source_description: Financial entities shall classify cyber threats as significant based on the criticality of the services at risk, including the financial entity’s transactions and operations, number and/or relevance of clients or financial counterparts targeted and the geographical spread of the areas at risk.
ccm_controls: GRC-02; BCR-02; BCR-03; SEF-02; SEF-06; SEF-07; SEF-08; TVM-04
addendum:
Missing specification(s) in the CCM v4.1: 
"including the financial entity’s transactions and operations, number and/or relevance of clients or financial counterparts targeted and the geographical spread of the areas at risk."
analysis: While CCM has robust threat and risk management, DORA provides specific, mandatory criteria for classifying cyber threats as significant (distinct from incidents). CCM does not explicitly require classification of threats based on "criticality of services at risk," "number/relevance of clients targeted," or "geographical spread of areas at risk" as mandatory factors for determining threat significance.

source_description:
Financial entities shall report major ICT-related incidents to the relevant competent authority as referred to in Article 46 in accordance with paragraph 4 of this Article.

Where a financial entity is subject to supervision by more than one national competent authority referred to in Article 46, Member States shall designate a single competent authority as the relevant competent authority responsible for carrying out the functions and duties provided for in this Article.

Credit institutions classified as significant, in accordance with Article 6(4) of Regulation (EU) No 1024/2013, shall report major ICT-related incidents to the relevant national competent authority designated in accordance with Article 4 of Directive 2013/36/EU which shall immediately transmit that report to the ECB. 

For the purpose of the first subparagraph, financial entities shall produce, after collecting and analysing all relevant information, the initial notification and reports referred to in paragraph 4 of this Article using the templates referred to in Article 20 and submit them to the competent authority. In the event that a technical impossibility prevents the submission of the initial notification using the template, financial entities shall notify the competent authority about it via alternative means.

The initial notification and reports referred to in paragraph 4 shall include all information necessary for the competent authority to determine the significance of the major ICT-related incident and assess possible cross-border impacts. 

Without prejudice to the reporting pursuant to the first subparagraph by the financial entity to the relevant competent authority, Member States may additionally determine that some or all financial entities shall also provide the initial notification and each report referred to in paragraph 4 of this Article using the templates referred to in Article 20 to the competent authorities or the computer security incident response teams (CSIRTs) designated or established in accordance with Directive (EU) 2022/2555.
addendum: Recommend that CCM uses the full DORA provision to close the gap. The mapped CCM controls cover in part the high specificity of the DORA provision objective.
analysis:
SEF-03 states, "Establish, document, approve, communicate, apply, evaluate, and maintain a security incident response plan, which includes but is not limited to: a communication strategy for notifying relevant internal departments, impacted service customers, and other business critical relationships (such as supply chain) that may be impacted."

SEF-10 states, "Maintain points of contact for applicable regulation authorities, national and local law enforcement, and other legal jurisdictional authorities."

Although a communication strategy and contacts with authorities are foreseen by controls SEF-03 and SEF-10, there is no obligation of immediate notification of an initial report in case of major incident.

source_description:
Financial entities may, on a voluntary basis, notify significant cyber threats to the relevant competent authority when they deem the threat to be of relevance to the financial system, service users or clients. The relevant competent authority may provide such information to other relevant authorities referred to in paragraph 6.

Credit institutions classified as significant, in accordance with Article 6(4) of Regulation (EU) No 1024/2013, may, on a voluntary basis, notify significant cyber threats to relevant national competent authority, designated in accordance with Article 4 of Directive 2013/36/EU, which shall immediately transmit the notification to the ECB.

Member States may determine that those financial entities that on a voluntary basis notify in accordance with the first subparagraph may also transmit that notification to the CSIRTs designated or established in accordance with Directive (EU) 2022/2555.
addendum: Recommend that CCM uses the full DORA provision to close the gap. The mapped CCM controls cover in part the high specificity of the DORA provision objective.
