analysis:
TVM-01 states, "Establish, document, approve, communicate, apply, evaluate, and maintain policies and procedures to identify, report, and prioritize the remediation of vulnerabilities and threats, in order to protect systems against vulnerability exploitation."

SEF-10 states, "Maintain points of contact for applicable regulation authorities, national and local law enforcement, and other legal jurisdictional authorities."

Although the detection and reporting of the remediation of threats and the contact with regulation authorities is mentioned in the CCM framework, the option to voluntary disclose information about significant threats is not explicitly stated.

source_description:
Where a major ICT-related incident occurs and has an impact on the financial interests of clients, financial entities shall, without undue delay as soon as they become aware of it, inform their clients about the major ICT-related incident and about the measures that have been taken to mitigate the adverse effects of such incident.
In the case of a significant cyber threat, financial entities shall, where applicable, inform their clients that are potentially affected of any appropriate protection measures which the latter may consider taking.
addendum:
Missing specification(s) in the CCM v4.1: 
"In the case of a significant cyber threat, financial entities shall, where applicable, inform their clients that are potentially affected of any appropriate protection measures which the latter may consider taking."
analysis:
SEF-03 states, "Establish, document, approve, communicate, apply, evaluate and maintain a security incident response plan, which includes but is not limited to: a communication strategy for notifying relevant internal departments, impacted service customers, and other business critical relationships (such as supply-chain) that may be impacted." 

There are no provisions to inform clients about an incident without undue delay as well as to share cyber threats with clients.

source_description: Financial entities shall, within the time limits to be laid down in accordance with Article 20, first paragraph, point (a), point (ii), submit the following to the relevant competent authority: An initial notification.
addendum: Recommend that CCM uses the full DORA provision to close the gap. The mapped CCM controls cover in part the high specificity of the DORA provision objective.
analysis:
SEF-03 states, "Establish, document, approve, communicate, apply, evaluate, and maintain a security incident response plan, which includes but is not limited to: a communication strategy for notifying relevant internal departments, impacted service customers, and other business critical relationships (such as supply chain) that may be impacted."

SEF-10 states, "Maintain points of contact for applicable regulation authorities, national and local law enforcement, and other legal jurisdictional authorities."

Although the CCM framework mentions the reporting of incidents and contact with regulation authorities, it does not explicitly mention the initial notification of a major incident to the competent authority. Moreover, there is no explicit timeline for an initial notification.

source_description: Financial entities shall, within the time limits to be laid down in accordance with Article 20, first paragraph, point (a), point (ii), submit the following to the relevant competent authority: An intermediate report after the initial notification referred to in point (a), as soon as the status of the original incident has changed significantly or the handling of the major ICT-related incident has changed based on new information available, followed, as appropriate, by updated notifications every time a relevant status update is available, as well as upon a specific request of the competent authority;
addendum:
Missing specification(s) in the CCM v4.1: 
"An intermediate report after the initial notification referred to in point (a), as soon as the status of the original incident has changed significantly or the handling of the major ICT-related incident has changed based on new information available, followed, as appropriate, by updated notifications every time a relevant status update is available, as well as upon a specific request of the competent authority."
analysis:
SEF-03 states, "Establish, document, approve, communicate, apply, evaluate, and maintain a security incident response plan, which includes but is not limited to: a communication strategy for notifying relevant internal departments, impacted service customers, and other business critical relationships (such as supply-chain) that may be impacted."

SEF-10 states, "Maintain points of contact for applicable regulation authorities, national and local law enforcement, and other legal jurisdictional authorities."

Although the CCM framework mentions the reporting of incidents and contact with regulation authorities, it does not explicitly mention the initial notification of a major incident to the competent authority. Moreover, there is no explicit timeline for an initial notification.

source_description: Financial entities shall, within the time limits to be laid down in accordance with Article 20, first paragraph, point (a), point (ii), submit the following to the relevant competent authority: A final report, when the root cause analysis has been completed, regardless of whether mitigation measures have already been implemented, and when the actual impact figures are available to replace estimates.
addendum:
Missing specification(s) in the CCM v4.1: 
"A final report, when the root cause analysis has been completed, regardless of whether mitigation measures have already been implemented, and when the actual impact figures are available to replace estimates."
analysis:
SEF-03 states, "Establish, document, approve, communicate, apply, evaluate, and maintain a security incident response plan, which includes but is not limited to: a communication strategy for notifying relevant internal departments, impacted service customers, and other business critical relationships (such as supply-chain) that may be impacted." 

SEF-09 states, "Establish and maintain a secure repository of security incident records. Regularly review the incident records to identify patterns, root causes, and systemic vulnerabilities, and implement relevant corrective measures."

SEF-10 states, "Maintain points of contact for applicable regulation authorities, national and local law enforcement, and other legal jurisdictional authorities."

Although the CCM framework mentions the reporting of incidents and contact with regulation authorities as well as the analysis of the root causes, it does not explicitly mention the submission of a final report about a major incident to the competent authority. Moreover, there is no explicit timeline for the submission of the final report.

source_description: Financial entities may outsource, in accordance with Union and national sectoral law, the reporting obligations under this Article to a third-party service provider. In case of such outsourcing, the financial entity remains fully responsible for the fulfilment of the incident reporting requirements.
addendum:
Missing specification(s) in the CCM v4.1: 
"in accordance with Union and national sectoral law, the reporting obligations under this Article to a third-party service provider."
analysis: Not applicable as it is a voluntary decision.

source_description: For the purpose of assessing preparedness for handling ICT-related incidents, of identifying weaknesses, deficiencies and gaps in digital operational resilience, and of promptly implementing corrective measures, financial entities, other than microenterprises, shall, taking into account the criteria set out in Article 4(2), establish, maintain and review a sound and comprehensive digital operational resilience testing programme as an integral part of the ICT risk-management framework referred to in Article 6.
ccm_controls: GRC-02; GRC-05; BCR-01; BCR-04; BCR-06; SEF-02; SEF-07
addendum:
Missing specification(s) in the CCM v4.1: 
"establish, maintain and review a sound and comprehensive digital operational resilience testing programme."
analysis: Incident Management (SEF) and Vulnerability Management (TVM) touch on some of the requirements for this paragraph but largely miss the requirement for a "digital operational resilience testing program," which implies specific testing around the operational resilience to threats. This means the organization should specifically perform a variety of security testing activities to evaluate whether detection, response, and recover controls are sufficiently protecting the organization from risks to operational capability.

source_description: The digital operational resilience testing programme shall include a range of assessments, tests, methodologies, practices and tools to be applied in accordance with Articles 25 and 26.
addendum: Recommend that CCM uses the full DORA provision to close the gap. The mapped CCM controls cover in part the high specificity of the DORA provision objective.
analysis: The CCM does not require a range of assessment types to evaluate the performance of operational resilience controls. The only one specified that might map to this requirement is Business Continuity Exercises (BCR-06).

source_description: When conducting the digital operational resilience testing programme referred to in paragraph 1 of this Article, financial entities, other than microenterprises, shall follow a risk-based approach taking into account the criteria set out in Article 4(2) duly considering the evolving landscape of ICT risk, any specific risks to which the financial entity concerned is or might be exposed, the criticality of information assets and of services provided, as well as any other factor the financial entity deems appropriate.
addendum:
Missing specification(s) in the CCM v4.1: 
"conducting the digital operational resilience testing programme."
analysis: Because there is no requirement in the CCM to conduct digital operational resilience testing, there is a partial gap. The requirements in BCR-01, TVM-10, and GRC-02 could provide sufficient coverage for the requirements in DORA if they are scoped to also be required to provide context to the "digital operational resilience testing programme."

source_description: Financial entities, other than microenterprises, shall ensure that tests are undertaken by independent parties, whether internal or external. Where tests are undertaken by an internal tester, financial entities shall dedicate sufficient resources and ensure that conflicts of interest are avoided throughout the design and execution phases of the test.
addendum:
Missing specification(s) in the CCM v4.1: 
"Where tests are undertaken by an internal tester, financial entities shall dedicate sufficient resources and ensure that conflicts of interest are avoided throughout the design and execution phases of the test."

source_description: Financial entities, other than microenterprises, shall establish procedures and policies to prioritise, classify and remedy all issues revealed throughout the performance of the tests and shall establish internal validation methodologies to ascertain that all identified weaknesses, deficiencies or gaps are fully addressed.
Financial entities, other than microenterprises, shall ensure, at least yearly, that appropriate tests are conducted on all ICT systems and applications supporting critical or important functions.

The digital operational resilience testing programme referred to in Article 24 shall provide, in accordance with the criteria set out in Article 4(2), for the execution of appropriate tests, such as vulnerability assessments and scans, open source analyses, network security assessments, gap analyses, physical security reviews, questionnaires and scanning software solutions, source code reviews where feasible, scenario–based tests, compatibility testing, performance testing, end–to–end testing and penetration testing.
ccm_controls: A&A-02; A&A-03; TVM-03; TVM-06; TVM-07; STA-13; AIS-05; BCR-06; UEM-03
addendum:
Missing specification(s) in the CCM v4.1: 
"such as vulnerability assessments and scans, open source analyses, network security assessments, gap analyses, physical security reviews, questionnaires and scanning software solutions, source code reviews where feasible, scenario-based tests, compatibility testing, performance testing, end-to-end testing and penetration testing."
analysis:
TVM-03 covers vulnerability assessments and scans.
TVM-06 covers that scanning should be conducted on third party libraries and open source code but no source code review.
TVM-07 covers penetration tests and could cover network security assessments and penetration tests.
A&A-02 arguably covers gap analysis, but it's not specific to gap analysis.
STA-13 covers supplier security assessments but not open source analysis.
AIS-05 covers application testing but does not specify source code reviews or open source analysis.
BCR-06 covers business continuity exercises, which could be scenario based but aren't necessarily.
UEM-03 covers endpoint compatibility, but that's only one small subset of compatibility testing.

No mention of end-to-end testing, scenario-based tests, open source analysis, source code reviews, or software compatibility.

source_description: Central securities depositories and central counterparties shall perform vulnerability assessments before any deployment or redeployment of new or existing applications and infrastructure components, and ICT services supporting critical or important functions of the financial entity.

Microenterprises shall perform the tests referred to in paragraph 1 by combining a risk-based approach with a strategic planning of ICT testing, by duly considering the need to maintain a balanced approach between the scale of resources and the time to be allocated to the ICT testing provided for in this Article, on the one hand, and the urgency, type of risk, criticality of information assets and of services provided, as well as any other relevant factor, including the financial entity’s ability to take calculated risks, on the other hand.
addendum:
Missing specification(s) in the CCM v4.1: 
"maintain a balanced approach between the scale of resources and the time to be allocated to the ICT testing provided for in this Article."
analysis: There is no explicit requirement to perform testing using a risk-based approach, but GRC-02 arguably could be used to determine what testing is appropriate for your risk appetite.

source_description: Financial entities, other than entities referred to in Article 16(1), first subparagraph, and other than microenterprises, which are identified in accordance with paragraph 8, third subparagraph, of this Article, shall carry out at least every 3 years advanced testing by means of TLPT. Based on the risk profile of the financial entity and taking into account operational circumstances, the competent authority may, where necessary, request the financial entity to reduce or increase this frequency.
addendum: Recommend that CCM uses the full DORA provision to close the gap. The mapped CCM controls cover in part the high specificity of the DORA provision objective.
analysis: A Threat-Led Penetration Test (TLPT) is a rigidly defined structure aligned with the TIBER-EU testing framework, which mandates significantly more structure in evaluation. The TIBER-EU framework requires five separate teams: blue team, threat intelligence providers, red-team testers, control team, and the TIBER cyber team. Each of these teams has a separate role in the TLPT, and the TLPT proceeds in a rigidly structured flow: initiation, scoping, threat intelligence, red-team testing, blue-team reporting, and remediation planning. The CCM does not refer to any such structure, and the usage of the generic term "penetration testing" in TVM-07 could not reasonably be interpreted to cover this strict requirement. This requirement is outlined in Paragraph 11 of this Article (which is properly out-scoped, but includes relevant information).

source_description:
Each threat-led penetration test shall cover several or all critical or important functions of a financial entity, and shall be performed on live production systems supporting such functions.
Financial entities shall identify all relevant underlying ICT systems, processes and technologies supporting critical or important functions and ICT services, including those supporting the critical or important functions which have been outsourced or contracted to ICT third-party service providers.
Financial entities shall assess which critical or important functions need to be covered by the TLPT. The result of this assessment shall determine the precise scope of TLPT and shall be validated by the competent authorities.
addendum: Recommend that CCM uses the full DORA provision to close the gap. The mapped CCM controls cover in part the high specificity of the DORA provision objective.
analysis:
Regulatory Oversight: No CCM control addresses validation or adjustment by competent authorities.
Live Environment Testing: CCM lacks mandates for testing in production environments.
Third-Party Enforcement: CCM does not enforce third-party participation in TLPT.
Advanced TLPT Methodology: CCM does not require threat intelligence or red teaming.
Formal Scope Definition: CCM supports risk assessment but lacks formal scope-setting tied to critical functions.

source_description: Where ICT third-party service providers are included in the scope of TLPT, the financial entity shall take the necessary measures and safeguards to ensure the participation of such ICT third-party service providers in the TLPT and shall retain at all times full responsibility for ensuring compliance with this Regulation.
addendum: Recommend that CCM uses the full DORA provision to close the gap. The mapped CCM controls cover in part the high specificity of the DORA provision objective.

source_description:
Without prejudice to paragraph 2, first and second subparagraphs, where the participation of an ICT third-party service provider in the TLPT, referred to in paragraph 3, is reasonably expected to have an adverse impact on the quality or security of services delivered by the ICT third-party service provider to customers that are entities falling outside the scope of this Regulation, or on the confidentiality of the data related to such services, the financial entity and the ICT third-party service provider may agree in writing that the ICT third-party service provider directly enters into contractual arrangements with an external tester, for the purpose of conducting, under the direction of one designated financial entity, a pooled TLPT involving several financial entities (pooled testing) to which the ICT third-party service provider provides ICT services. That pooled testing shall cover the relevant range of ICT services supporting critical or important functions contracted to the respective ICT third-party service provider by the financial entities. The pooled testing shall be considered TLPT carried out by the financial entities participating in the pooled testing.
The number of financial entities participating in the pooled testing shall be duly calibrated taking into account the complexity and types of services involved.
addendum: Recommend that CCM uses the full DORA provision to close the gap. The mapped CCM controls cover in part the high specificity of the DORA provision objective.

source_description: Financial entities shall, with the cooperation of ICT third-party service providers and other parties involved, including the testers but excluding the competent authorities, apply effective risk management controls to mitigate the risks of any potential impact on data, damage to assets, and disruption to critical or important functions, services or operations at the financial entity itself, its counterparts or to the financial sector.
addendum: Recommend that CCM uses the full DORA provision to close the gap. The mapped CCM controls cover in part the high specificity of the DORA provision objective.

source_description: At the end of the testing, after reports and remediation plans have been agreed, the financial entity and, where applicable, the external testers shall provide to the authority, designated in accordance with paragraph 9 or 10, a summary of the relevant findings, the remediation plans and the documentation demonstrating that the TLPT has been conducted in accordance with the requirements.
addendum: Recommend that CCM uses the full DORA provision to close the gap. The mapped CCM controls cover in part the high specificity of the DORA provision objective.

source_description:
Authorities shall provide financial entities with an attestation confirming that the test was performed in accordance with the requirements as evidenced in the documentation in order to allow for mutual recognition of threat led penetration tests between competent authorities. The financial entity shall notify the relevant competent authority of the attestation, the summary of the relevant findings and the remediation plans.
Without prejudice to such attestation, financial entities shall remain at all times fully responsible for the impact of the tests referred to in paragraph 4.
addendum: Recommend that CCM uses the full DORA provision to close the gap. The mapped CCM controls cover in part the high specificity of the DORA provision objective.

source_description:
Financial entities shall contract testers for the purposes of undertaking TLPT in accordance with Article 27. When financial entities use internal testers for the purposes of undertaking TLPT, they shall contract external testers every three tests.
Credit institutions that are classified as significant in accordance with Article 6(4) of Regulation (EU) No 1024/2013, shall only use external testers in accordance with Article 27(1), points (a) to (e).
addendum: Recommend that CCM uses the full DORA provision to close the gap. The mapped CCM controls cover in part the high specificity of the DORA provision objective.

source_description: Financial entities shall only use testers for the carrying out of TLPT, which are of the highest suitability and reputability;
addendum:
Missing specification(s) in the CCM v4.1: 
"[testers] are of the highest suitability and reputability"
analysis:
While CCM requires independent pen testing like DORA, CCM does not require pen testers be of the highest suitability and reputability. There is, therefore, at least a partial gap.

Companies should note that while pen testing is required in both CCM and DORA, DORA has additional requirements for testers. Companies should therefore assess the suitability and reputability of the third-party pen testers to bridge the gap.

source_description: Financial entities shall only use testers for the carrying out of TLPT, which possess technical and organisational capabilities and demonstrate specific expertise in threat intelligence, penetration testing and red team testing;
addendum: Recommend that CCM uses the full DORA provision to close the gap. The mapped CCM controls cover in part the high specificity of the DORA provision objective.
analysis:
While pen testing is referred to in CCM and DORA, DORA goes further, requiring an assessment of the pen tester's capabilities and expertise. This is at least a partial gap.

Companies should note that there is at least a partial gap as DORA goes further than CCM. The gap can be bridged by assessing and ensuring that the third-party pen testers have adequate technical and organizational capabilities and expertise in pen testing.

source_description: Financial entities shall only use testers for the carrying out of TLPT, which are certified by an accreditation body in a Member State or adhere to formal codes of conduct or ethical frameworks;
addendum: Recommend that CCM uses the full DORA provision to close the gap. The mapped CCM controls cover in part the high specificity of the DORA provision objective.
analysis: In order to bridge the gap between CCM and DORA, companies will need to ensure that their external pen testers are certified and accredited by an appropriate body in the EU or alternatively adhere to an appropriate code deemed appropriate in the EU.

source_description: Financial entities shall only use testers for the carrying out of TLPT, which provide an independent assurance, or an audit report, in relation to the sound management of risks associated with the carrying out of TLPT, including the due protection of the financial entity’s confidential information and redress for the business risks of the financial entity;
addendum: Recommend that CCM uses the full DORA provision to close the gap. The mapped CCM controls cover in part the high specificity of the DORA provision objective.
analysis:
While independent third-party testing is required by both CCM and DORA, DORA is more specific in the requirements and outputs from the pen tester.

Companies should note that while pen testing is required under both CCM and DORA, the requirements for pen testers are more detailed in DORA. For this criterion, companies will need to ensure that the outputs from the pen tester offer independent assurance or an audit report for the pen testing process, protection of the entity's data, and redress for business risks. These may require additional contract terms when hiring the pen tester but should not present an onerous impediment for companies.

source_description: Financial entities shall only use testers for the carrying out of TLPT, which are duly and fully covered by relevant professional indemnity insurances, including against risks of misconduct and negligence.
addendum: Recommend that CCM uses the full DORA provision to close the gap. The mapped CCM controls cover in part the high specificity of the DORA provision objective.
analysis: As DORA goes further than CCM in this regard, companies will need to ensure that the external pen tester has the appropriate insurance, as required under DORA. This is a check, but companies, in addition, may also consider requiring this in appropriate contract clauses.

source_description: When using internal testers, financial entities shall ensure that, in addition to the requirements in paragraph 1, the following conditions are met: Such use has been approved by the relevant competent authority or by the single public authority designated in accordance with Article 26(9) and (10);
addendum: The full DORA provision is missing from CCM v4.1 and has to be used to close the gap.
analysis: As DORA is more detailed in this regard, companies should consider that the internal pen testers satisfy the above requirements, the below requirements, and any requirements of the competent authority in order to fill the gap. These will need to be assessed in advance and verified as appropriate.

source_description: When using internal testers, financial entities shall ensure that, in addition to the requirements in paragraph 1, the following conditions are met: The relevant competent authority has verified that the financial entity has sufficient dedicated resources and ensured that conflicts of interest are avoided throughout the design and execution phases of the test;
addendum: The full DORA provision is missing from CCM v4.1 and has to be used to close the gap.
analysis: DORA is more detailed in this regard. In order to bridge the gap, companies using internal pen testers should ensure that the competent authority agrees that the company has sufficient resources for the exercise and that conflicts are avoided, in addition to the above requirements being satisfied.

source_description: When using internal testers, financial entities shall ensure that, in addition to the requirements in paragraph 1, the following conditions are met: The threat intelligence provider is external to the financial entity.
addendum: The full DORA provision is missing from CCM v4.1 and has to be used to close the gap.
analysis: DORA is more detailed in relation to pen testing, external and internal. In order to bridge the gap for internal pen testers (assuming all other requirements are satisfied), the provision of threat analysis is independent of the internal pen tester and also provided from an external source.

source_description: Financial entities shall ensure that contracts concluded with external testers require a sound management of the TLPT results and that any data processing thereof, including any generation, store, aggregation, draft, report, communication or destruction, do not create risks to the financial entity.
addendum: The full DORA provision is missing from CCM v4.1 and has to be used to close the gap.
analysis: DORA is more detailed than CCM in this regard. However, to satisfy DORA, companies should have contracts in place with their external pen testers. As this should be the case in any event, this part should then just be an additional check. However, contracts should be reviewed to also ensure that the specific contract requirements of DORA are included. If not included, appropriate updates can be considered. Once in place, this will have satisfied DORA in this regard.

source_description: Financial entities shall manage ICT third-party risk as an integral component of ICT risk within their ICT risk management framework as referred to in Article 6(1), and in accordance with financial entities that have in place contractual arrangements for the use of ICT services to run their business operations shall, at all times, remain fully responsible for compliance with, and the discharge of, all obligations under this Regulation and applicable financial services law;
addendum:
Missing specification(s) in the CCM v4.1: 
"at all times, remain fully responsible for compliance with, and the discharge of, all obligations under this Regulation and applicable financial services law."
analysis:
Both frameworks have the requirement in place to manage risks associated with ICT third-party or supply chain relationships.

CCM lacks a requirement that the ICT third-party risk management must be an integral component of ICT risk within the financial entities' ICT risk management framework.

CCM lacks the requirement that financial entities shall, at all times, remain fully responsible for compliance with, and the discharge of, all obligations under this regulation and applicable financial services law.

source_description: Financial entities shall manage ICT third-party risk as an integral component of ICT risk within their ICT risk management framework as referred to in Article 6(1), and in accordance with financial entities’ management of ICT third-party risk shall be implemented in light of the principle of proportionality, taking into account the nature, scale, complexity and importance of ICT-related dependencies,
addendum:
Missing specification(s) in the CCM v4.1: 
"in light of the principle of proportionality, taking into account the nature, scale, complexity and importance of ICT-related dependencies."
analysis: CCM lacks a requirement that the management of ICT third-party risk must consider the nature, scale, complexity, and importance of dependencies, which is not as explicitly defined in the CCM. The CCM provides a general framework for risk management without the same level of detail regarding proportionality.

source_description: Financial entities shall manage ICT third-party risk as an integral component of ICT risk within their ICT risk management framework as referred to in Article 6(1), and in accordance with financial entities’ management of ICT third-party risk shall be implemented in light of the principle of proportionality, taking into account the risks arising from contractual arrangements on the use of ICT services concluded with ICT third-party service providers, taking into account the criticality or importance of the respective service, process or function, and the potential impact on the continuity and availability of financial services and activities, at individual and at group level.
addendum:
Missing specification(s) in the CCM v4.1: 
"in light of the principle of proportionality."

source_description: As part of their ICT risk management framework, financial entities, other than entities referred to in Article 16(1), first subparagraph, and other than microenterprises, shall adopt, and regularly review, a strategy on ICT third-party risk, taking into account the multi-vendor strategy referred to in Article 6(9), where applicable. The strategy on ICT third-party risk shall include a policy on the use of ICT services supporting critical or important functions provided by ICT third-party service providers and shall apply on an individual basis and, where relevant, on a sub-consolidated and consolidated basis. The management body shall, on the basis of an assessment of the overall risk profile of the financial entity and the scale and complexity of the business services, regularly review the risks identified in respect to contractual arrangements on the use of ICT services supporting critical or important functions.
addendum:
Missing specification(s) in the CCM v4.1: 
"shall apply on an individual basis and, where relevant, on a sub-consolidated and consolidated basis."

source_description:
As part of their ICT risk management framework, financial entities shall maintain and update at entity level, and at sub-consolidated and consolidated levels, a register of information in relation to all contractual arrangements on the use of ICT services provided by ICT third-party service providers.

The contractual arrangements referred to in the first subparagraph shall be appropriately documented, distinguishing between those that cover ICT services supporting critical or important functions and those that do not.

Financial entities shall report at least yearly to the competent authorities on the number of new arrangements on the use of ICT services, the categories of ICT third-party service providers, the type of contractual arrangements and the ICT services and functions which are being provided.

Financial entities shall make available to the competent authority, upon its request, the full register of information or, as requested, specified sections thereof, along with any information deemed necessary to enable the effective supervision of the financial entity.

Financial entities shall inform the competent authority in a timely manner about any planned contractual arrangement on the use of ICT services supporting critical or important functions as well as when a function has become critical or important.
addendum:
Missing specification(s) in the CCM v4.1: 
"at sub-consolidated and consolidated levels,"
"distinguishing between those that cover ICT services supporting critical or important functions and those that do not,"
"Financial entities shall report at least yearly to the competent authorities on the number of new arrangements on the use of ICT services, the categories of ICT third-party service providers, the type of contractual arrangements and the ICT services and functions which are being provided,"
"Financial entities shall make available to the competent authority, upon its request, the full register of information or, as requested, specified sections thereof, along with any information deemed necessary to enable the effective supervision of the financial entity," and
"Financial entities shall inform the competent authority in a timely manner about any planned contractual arrangement on the use of ICT services supporting critical or important functions as well as when a function has become critical or important."
analysis:
Both frameworks require the development and maintenance of a register or inventory of  all contractual arrangements with ICT third-party service providers. 

CCM lacks the inclusion of the register to the overall ICT risk management framework. CCM lacks precise requirements on the form and content of the register or inventory. These are: maintaining the register/inventory at entity level, and at sub-consolidated and consolidated levels; and distinction between contractual arrangements that cover ICT services supporting critical or important functions and those that do not.

CCM lacks reporting and information obligations towards the competent authorities. These are: report at least yearly on the number of new arrangements on the use of ICT services, the categories of ICT third-party service providers, the type of contractual arrangements, and the ICT services and functions that are being provided; upon its request, make available the full register of information or, as requested, specified sections thereof, along with any information deemed necessary to enable the effective supervision of the financial entity; and inform in a timely manner about any planned contractual arrangement on the use of ICT services supporting critical or important functions as well as when a function has become critical or important.

source_description: Before entering into a contractual arrangement on the use of ICT services, financial entities shall assess whether the contractual arrangement covers the use of ICT services supporting a critical or important function;
analysis:
CCM requires a periodic review of risk factors associated with supply chain relationships.

CCM lacks the requirement to do this review before entering into the contractual arrangement.

CCM also lacks the specific review regarding whether the contractual arrangement covers the use of ICT services supporting a critical or important function.

source_description: Before entering into a contractual arrangement on the use of ICT services, financial entities shall assess if supervisory conditions for contracting are met;
addendum:
Missing specification(s) in the CCM v4.1: 
"assess if supervisory conditions for contracting are met."
analysis:
CCM requires a periodic review of risk factors associated with supply chain relationships.

CCM lacks the specific review regarding whether supervisory conditions for contracting are met.

source_description: Before entering into a contractual arrangement on the use of ICT services, financial entities shall identify and assess all relevant risks in relation to the contractual arrangement, including the possibility that such contractual arrangement may contribute to reinforcing ICT concentration risk as referred to in Article 29;
addendum:
Missing specification(s) in the CCM v4.1: 
"identify and assess...the possibility that such contractual arrangement may contribute to reinforcing ICT concentration risk as referred to in Article 29."
analysis:
CCM requires a periodic review of risk factors associated with supply chain relationships.

CCM lacks the specific review regarding the possibility that such contractual arrangement may contribute to reinforcing ICT concentration risk.

source_description: Before entering into a contractual arrangement on the use of ICT services, financial entities shall undertake all due diligence on prospective ICT third-party service providers and ensure throughout the selection and assessment processes that the ICT third-party service provider is suitable;
analysis: CCM requires a periodic review of risk factors associated with supply chain relationships, which involves a due diligence as required by DORA.

source_description: Before entering into a contractual arrangement on the use of ICT services, financial entities shall identify and assess conflicts of interest that the contractual arrangement may cause.
addendum:
Missing specification(s) in the CCM v4.1: 
"shall identify and assess conflicts of interest that the contractual arrangement may cause."
analysis:
CCM requires a periodic review of risk factors associated with supply chain relationships.

CCM lacks the specific review and identification of conflicts of interest that the contractual arrangement may cause.

source_description: Financial entities may only enter into contractual arrangements with ICT third-party service providers that comply with appropriate information security standards. When those contractual arrangements concern critical or important functions, financial entities shall, prior to concluding the arrangements, take due consideration of the use, by ICT third-party service providers, of the most up-to-date and highest quality information security standards.
addendum:
Missing specification(s) in the CCM v4.1: 
"financial entities shall...take due consideration of the use, by ICT third-party service providers, of the most up-to-date and highest quality information security standards."
analysis:
CCM requires a periodic review of risk factors associated with supply chain relationships.

CCM lacks the specific requirement that financial entities are only allowed to enter into a contractual arrangement with ICT third-party service providers that comply with appropriate information security standards.

CCM also lacks the review before entering into a contractual arrangement whether a third-party service provider that supports critical or important functions applies the most up-to-date and highest quality information security standards.

source_description:
In exercising access, inspection and audit rights over the ICT third-party service provider, financial entities shall, on the basis of a risk-based approach, pre-determine the frequency of audits and inspections as well as the areas to be audited through adhering to commonly accepted audit standards in line with any supervisory instruction on the use and incorporation of such audit standards. 

Where contractual arrangements concluded with ICT third-party service providers on the use of ICT services entail high technical complexity, the financial entity shall verify that auditors, whether internal or external, or a pool of auditors, possess appropriate skills and knowledge to effectively perform the relevant audits and assessments.
addendum:
Missing specification(s) in the CCM v4.1: 
"pre-determine the frequency of audits and inspections as well as the areas to be audited through adhering to commonly accepted audit standards in line with any supervisory instruction on the use and incorporation of such audit standards" and
"the financial entity shall verify that auditors, whether internal or external, or a pool of auditors, possess appropriate skills and knowledge to effectively perform the relevant audits and assessments."
analysis:
CCM requires the right to audit as part of the service agreement with the third-party service provider. This requirement corresponds with the DORA requirement.

CCM lacks specifications regarding the audit: the risk-based approach, the frequency, areas to be audited, adherence to audit standards, and the qualifications of auditors.

CCM lacks specifications regarding the audit on the use of ICT services that entail high technical complexity: the need for auditors to have appropriate skills and knowledge.

source_description: Financial entities shall ensure that contractual arrangements on the use of ICT services may be terminated by significant breach by the ICT third-party service provider of applicable laws, regulations or contractual terms;
addendum: Recommend that CCM uses the full DORA provision to close the gap. The mapped CCM controls cover in part the high specificity of the DORA provision objective.
analysis:
CCM requires service termination as part of the service agreement with the third-party service provider. This requirement corresponds with the DORA requirement.

CCM lacks the specific termination condition: in case of a significant breach by the ICT third-party service provider of applicable laws, regulations, or contractual terms.

source_description: Financial entities shall ensure that contractual arrangements on the use of ICT services may be terminated by circumstances identified throughout the monitoring of ICT third-party risk that are deemed capable of altering the performance of the functions provided through the contractual arrangement, including material changes that affect the arrangement or the situation of the ICT third-party service provider;
addendum:
Missing specification(s) in the CCM v4.1: 
"ICT services may be terminated by circumstances...that are deemed capable of altering the performance of the functions provided through the contractual arrangement, including material changes that affect the arrangement or the situation of the ICT third-party service provider."
analysis:
CCM requires service termination as part of the service agreement with the third-party service provider. This requirement corresponds with the DORA requirement.

CCM lacks on the specific termination condition: in case of circumstances identified throughout the monitoring of ICT third-party risk that are deemed capable of altering the performance of the functions provided through the contractual arrangement, including material changes that affect the arrangement or the situation of the ICT third-party service provider.

source_description: Financial entities shall ensure that contractual arrangements on the use of ICT services may be terminated by ICT third-party service provider’s evidenced weaknesses pertaining to its overall ICT risk management and in particular in the way it ensures the availability, authenticity, integrity and, confidentiality, of data, whether personal or otherwise sensitive data, or non-personal data;
addendum:
Missing specification(s) in the CCM v4.1: 
"overall ICT risk management and in particular in the way it ensures the availability, authenticity, integrity and, confidentiality, of data, whether personal or otherwise sensitive data, or non-personal data."
analysis:
CCM requires service termination as part of the service agreement with the third-party service provider. This requirement corresponds with the DORA requirement.

CCM lacks on the specific termination condition: in case of ICT third-party service provider’s evidenced weaknesses pertaining to its overall ICT risk management and in particular in the way it ensures the availability, authenticity, integrity and, confidentiality, of data, whether personal or otherwise sensitive data, or non-personal data.

source_description: Financial entities shall ensure that contractual arrangements on the use of ICT services may be terminated where the competent authority can no longer effectively supervise the financial entity as a result of the conditions of, or circumstances related to, the respective contractual arrangement.
addendum:

"the competent authority can no longer effectively supervise the financial entity as a result of the conditions of, or circumstances related to, the respective contractual arrangement."
analysis:
CCM requires service termination as part of the service agreement with the third-party service provider. This requirement corresponds with the DORA requirement.

CCM lacks on the specific termination condition: where the competent authority can no longer effectively supervise the financial entity as a result of the conditions of, or circumstances related to, the respective contractual arrangement.

source_description: For ICT services supporting critical or important functions, financial entities shall put in place exit strategies. The exit strategies shall take into account risks that may emerge at the level of ICT third-party service providers, in particular a possible failure on their part, a deterioration of the quality of the ICT services provided, any business disruption due to inappropriate or failed provision of ICT services or any material risk arising in relation to the appropriate and continuous deployment of the respective ICT service, or the termination of contractual arrangements with ICT third-party service providers under any of the circumstances listed in paragraph 7.
ccm_controls: BCR-01; BCR-03; BCR-04; IPY-01; IPY-04; STA-10; STA-11; STA-16
addendum:
Missing specification(s) in the CCM v4.1: 
"For ICT services supporting critical or important functions, financial entities shall put in place exit strategies."
analysis:
BCR-01 requires business continuity management and operational resilience policies and procedures.

BCR-03 and BCR-04 require business continuity strategies and planning. Exit plans as required by DORA can be a specific product of these considerations but are not mentioned explicitly.

IPY-01 through IPY-04 set out specific technical requirements to ensure interoperability and portability also in the event of contract termination and address the need for agreements to specify access to data upon contract termination, which aligns with the concept of exit strategies in DORA.

CCM does not explicitly mention the requirements to put in place exit strategies for ICT services supporting critical or important functions provided by third-parties, or to consider the risks that may emerge at the level of ICT third-party service providers. In particular, a possible failure on their part, a deterioration of the quality of the ICT services provided, any business disruption due to inappropriate or failed provision of ICT services or any material risk arising in relation to the appropriate and continuous deployment of the respective ICT service, or the termination of contractual arrangements with ICT third-party service providers under any of the circumstances listed in paragraph 7.

source_description: Exit plans shall be comprehensive, documented and, in accordance with the criteria set out in Article 4(2), shall be sufficiently tested and reviewed periodically.
ccm_controls: BCR-01; BCR-03; BCR-04; BCR-05; BCR-06; IPY-01; IPY-04
addendum: Recommend that CCM uses the full DORA provision to close the gap. The mapped CCM controls cover in part the high specificity of the DORA provision objective.
analysis:
BCR-01 requires business continuity management and operational resilience policies and procedures.

BCR-03 and BCR-04 require business continuity strategies and planning. 

BCR-05 requires the documentation and annual review of documents relevant to support the business continuity and operational resilience programs. 

BCR-06 requires the testing of business continuity plans. Exit plans as required by DORA can be a specific product of these considerations but are not mentioned explicitly.

IPY-01 through IPY-04 set out specific technical requirements to ensure interoperability and portability also in the event of contract termination and address the need for agreements to specify access to data upon contract termination, which aligns with the concept of exit strategies in DORA.

CCM does not explicitly mention the requirements that the exit plans must be: comprehensive, documented, and in accordance with the criteria of the principle of proportionality (set out in Article 4(2)); sufficiently tested; and reviewed periodically.

source_description: Financial entities shall identify alternative solutions and develop transition plans enabling them to remove the contracted ICT services and the relevant data from the ICT third-party service provider and to securely and integrally transfer them to alternative providers or reincorporate them in-house.
Financial entities shall have appropriate contingency measures in place to maintain business continuity in the event of the circumstances referred to in the first subparagraph.

When performing the identification and assessment of risks referred to in Article 28(4), point (c), financial entities shall also take into account whether the envisaged conclusion of a contractual arrangement in relation to  ICT services supporting critical or important functions would lead to contracting an ICT third-party service provider that is not easily substitutable.
ccm_controls: STA-10; STA-11; STA-14; IPY-01; IPY-02; IPY-04
analysis: STA-10 requires companies to review risk factors associated with supply chain relationships, and STA-11 specifically mentions the need to include provisions for service termination in the service agreements. Furthermore, IPY-01, IPY-02, and IPY-04 require that controls be in place (i.e., policies and procedures) that allow data portability and interoperability, which mitigate the vendor lock-in risk.

source_description:
When performing the identification and assessment of risks referred to in Article 28(4), point (c), financial entities shall also take into account whether the envisaged conclusion of a contractual arrangement in relation to  ICT services supporting critical or important functions would lead to having in place multiple contractual arrangements in relation to the provision of ICT services supporting critical or important functions with the same ICT third-party service provider or with closely connected ICT third-party service providers.

Financial entities shall weigh the benefits and costs of alternative solutions, such as the use of different ICT third-party service providers, taking into account if and how envisaged solutions match the business needs and objectives set out in their digital resilience strategy.
addendum:
Missing specification(s) in the CCM v4.1:  
"having in place multiple contractual arrangements in relation to the provision of ICT services supporting critical or important functions with the same ICT third-party service provider or with closely connected ICT third-party service providers" and
"Financial entities shall weigh the benefits and costs of alternative solutions, such as the use of different ICT third-party service providers, taking into account if and how envisaged solutions match the business needs and objectives set out in their digital resilience strategy."
analysis: STA-10 requires companies to review risk factors associated with supply chain relationships, but the CCM does not specifically mention controls for mitigating concentration risk (i.e., relying on a single vendor for critical services, which creates a single point of failure).

source_description:
Where the contractual arrangements on the use of ICT services supporting critical or important functions include the possibility that an ICT third-party service provider further subcontracts ICT services supporting a critical or important function to other ICT third-party service providers, financial entities shall weigh benefits and risks that may arise in connection with such subcontracting, in particular in the case of an ICT subcontractor established in a third-country. 

Where contractual arrangements concern ICT services supporting critical or important functions, financial entities shall duly consider the insolvency law provisions that would apply in the event of the ICT third-party service provider’s bankruptcy as well as any constraint that may arise in respect to the urgent recovery of the financial entity’s data. 

Where contractual arrangements on the use of ICT services supporting critical or important functions are concluded with an ICT third-party service provider established in a third country, financial entities shall, in addition to the considerations referred to in the second subparagraph, also consider the compliance with Union data protection rules and the effective enforcement of the law in that third country. 

Where the contractual arrangements on the use of ICT services supporting critical or important functions provide for subcontracting, financial entities shall assess whether and how potentially long or complex chains of subcontracting may impact their ability to fully monitor the contracted functions and the ability of the competent authority to effectively supervise the financial entity in that respect.
addendum: Recommend that CCM uses the full DORA provision to close the gap. The mapped CCM controls cover in part the high specificity of the DORA provision objective.
analysis: While STA-10 and STA-11 say to periodically review risk factors associated with supply chain relationships, the CCM does not specifically have the requirements that DORA specifies in this paragraph (Article 29, Paragraph 2).

source_description: The rights and obligations of the financial entity and of the ICT third-party service provider shall be clearly allocated and set out in writing. The full contract shall include the service level agreements and be documented in one written document which shall be available to the parties on paper, or in a document with another downloadable, durable and accessible format.
addendum:
Missing specification(s) in the CCM v4.1:  
"The rights and obligations of the financial entity and of the ICT third-party service provider shall be clearly allocated and set out in writing. The full contract shall include the service level agreements and be documented in one written document which shall be available to the parties on paper, or in a document with another downloadable, durable and accessible format."
analysis: While STA-11 covers some of the provisions and terms to be considered in service agreements, it does not specify that all rights and obligations shall be allocated and set out in writing. Also, it does not specify that the contract should be available in paper or downloadable format.

source_description: The contractual arrangements on the use of ICT services shall include at least a clear and complete description of all functions and ICT services to be provided by the ICT third-party service provider, indicating whether subcontracting of an ICT service supporting a critical or important function, or material parts thereof, is permitted and, when that is the case, the conditions applying to such subcontracting;
addendum:
Missing specification(s) in the CCM v4.1:  
"The contractual arrangements on the use of ICT services shall indicate whether subcontracting of an ICT service supporting a critical or important function, or material parts thereof, is permitted and, when that is the case, the conditions applying to such subcontracting."
analysis: STA-11 does require that service agreements must incorporate services offered by the third-party service provider, but it does not require the contract to specify whether subcontracting of ICT services is permitted and conditions of such subcontracting.

source_description: The contractual arrangements on the use of ICT services shall include at least the locations, namely the regions or countries, where the contracted or subcontracted functions and ICT services are to be provided and where data is to be processed, including the storage location, and the requirement for the ICT third-party service provider to notify the financial entity in advance if it envisages changing such locations;
addendum:
Missing specification(s) in the CCM v4.1:  
"The contractual arrangements on the use of ICT services shall include at least the locations, namely the regions or countries, where data is to be processed, including the storage location, and the requirement for the ICT third-party service provider to notify the financial entity in advance if it envisages changing such locations."
analysis: While STA-11 requires that service agreements incorporate "location of business relationship," it does not require specifying the location where data would be processed and stored, nor does it require the third-party service provider to notify the financial entity of any changes in such locations.

source_description: The contractual arrangements on the use of ICT services shall include at least provisions on availability, authenticity, integrity and confidentiality in relation to the protection of data, including personal data;
addendum:
Missing specification(s) in the CCM v4.1:  
"The contractual arrangements on the use of ICT services shall include at least provisions on availability, authenticity, integrity and confidentiality in relation to the protection of data, including personal data."
analysis: STA-11 requires that service agreements must incorporate "information security requirements" but does not specify clearly to include provisions on availability, authenticity, integrity, and confidentiality in relation to the protection of data, including personal data.

source_description: The contractual arrangements on the use of ICT services shall include at least provisions on ensuring access, recovery and return in an easily accessible format of personal and non-personal data processed by the financial entity in the event of the insolvency, resolution or discontinuation of the business operations of the ICT third-party service provider, or in the event of the termination of the contractual arrangements;
addendum:
Missing specification(s) in the CCM v4.1:  
"The contractual arrangements on the use of ICT services shall include provisions to ensure access and recovery of data in the event of the insolvency, resolution or discontinuation of the business operations of the ICT third-party service provider."
analysis: IPY-04 specifies similar provisions for data access upon contract termination but does not specify that such provisions also are applicable in the event of insolvency, resolution, or discontinuation of the business operations of the third-party service provider.

source_description: The contractual arrangements on the use of ICT services shall include at least service level descriptions, including updates and revisions thereof;
addendum:
Missing specification(s) in the CCM v4.1:  
"The contractual arrangements on the use of ICT services shall include service level descriptions, including updates and revisions thereof."
analysis: STA-11 mentions that service agreements must incorporate services offered, but it does not specify to incorporate service level descriptions, including updates and revisions thereof.

source_description: The contractual arrangements on the use of ICT services shall include at least the obligation of the ICT third-party service provider to provide assistance to the financial entity at no additional cost, or at a cost that is determined ex-ante, when an ICT incident that is related to the ICT service provided to the financial entity occurs;
addendum:
Missing specification(s) in the CCM v4.1: 
"include at least the obligation of the ICT third-party service provider to provide assistance to the financial entity at no additional cost, or at a cost that is determined ex-ante, when an ICT incident that is related to the ICT service provided to the financial entity occurs."
analysis: Firms will need to consider the DORA additional requirement and how best to align. IT may require contract additions, or some of the elements may align in the wider contract framework and service descriptions in place at entity level.

source_description: The contractual arrangements on the use of ICT services shall include at least the obligation of the ICT third-party service provider to fully cooperate with the competent authorities and the resolution authorities of the financial entity, including persons appointed by them;
addendum:
Missing specification(s) in the CCM v4.1:  
"include at least the obligation of the ICT third-party service provider to fully cooperate with the competent authorities and the resolution authorities of the financial entity, including persons appointed by them."
analysis:
There is a particular context behind this DORA requirement, which is a backdrop in the rules and regulations of the financial services sector that specifies this consent. Relevant entities would need to add this to CCM to meet DORA requirements. However, those firms most directly affected may have this in mind already, regardless of CCM.

Add obligation of the third-party service provider to fully cooperate with the competent authorities and the resolution authorities of the financial entity, including persons appointed by authorities.

source_description: The contractual arrangements on the use of ICT services shall include at least termination rights and related minimum notice periods for the termination of the contractual arrangements, in accordance with the expectations of competent authorities and resolution authorities;
addendum:
Missing specification(s) in the CCM v4.1:  
"minimum notice periods for the termination of the contractual arrangements, in accordance with the expectations of competent authorities and resolution authorities."
analysis:
CCM is not as specific on this point, compared to DORA. Again, there is a financial services backdrop. It is also more focused on regulation than CCM on this point, envisaging regulatory supervision.

Add termination rights and related minimum notice periods for the termination of the contractual arrangements, in accordance with the expectations of competent authorities and resolution authorities.

source_description: The contractual arrangements on the use of ICT services shall include at least the conditions for the participation of ICT third-party service providers in the financial entities' ICT security awareness programmes and digital operational resilience training in accordance with Article 13(6).
addendum:
Missing specification(s) in the CCM v4.1:  
"digital operational resilience training."
analysis:
STA-14 requires compliance of third-party providers to "personnel policy," and STA-11 requires adherence to "information security requirements."
HRS-11 and HRS-12 include Security Awareness Training.

CCM has no reference to digital operational resilience training specifically.

source_description: The contractual arrangements on the use of ICT services supporting critical or important functions shall include, in addition to the elements referred to in paragraph 2, at least the full service level descriptions, including updates and revisions thereof with precise quantitative and qualitative performance targets within the agreed service levels to allow effective monitoring by the financial entity of ICT services and enable appropriate corrective actions to be taken, without undue delay, when agreed service levels are not met;
addendum:
Missing specification(s) in the CCM v4.1:  
"full service level descriptions, including updates and revisions thereof with precise quantitative and qualitative performance targets within the agreed service levels to allow effective monitoring by the financial entity of IT services and enable appropriate corrective actions to be taken, without undue delay, when agreed service levels are not met."
analysis: Add full service-level descriptions, including updates and revisions thereof with precise quantitative and qualitative performance targets within the agreed service levels to allow effective monitoring by the financial entity of IT services and enable appropriate corrective actions to be taken, without undue delay, when agreed service levels are not met.

source_description: The contractual arrangements on the use of ICT services supporting critical or important functions shall include, in addition to the elements referred to in paragraph 2, at least the notice periods and reporting obligations of the ICT third-party service provider to the financial entity, including notification of any development that might have a material impact on the ICT third-party service provider’s ability to effectively provide the ICT services supporting critical or important functions in line with agreed service levels;
addendum:
Missing specification(s) in the CCM v4.1:   
"notice periods and reporting obligations of the ICT third-party service provider to the financial entity, including notification of any development that might have a material impact on the ICT third-party service provider’s ability to effectively provide the ICT services supporting critical or important functions in line with agreed service levels."
analysis: STA-11 serves as a control that lists contractual provisions that are a must to have within a service agreement between cloud service provider (CSP) and cloud service customer (CSC), and thus is a valid mapping. Partial gap is due to certain specificities/details on the provisions that must be included.

source_description: The contractual arrangements on the use of ICT services supporting critical or important functions shall include, in addition to the elements referred to in paragraph 2, at least the requirements for the ICT third-party service provider to implement and test business contingency plans and to have in place ICT security measures, tools and policies that provide an appropriate level of security for the provision of services by the financial entity in line with its regulatory framework;
addendum:
Missing specification(s) in the CCM v4.1:  
"the requirements for the ICT third-party service provider to implement and test business contingency plans and to have in place ICT security measures, tools and policies that provide an appropriate level of security for the provision of services by the financial entity in line with its regulatory framework."

addendum:
Missing specification(s) in the CCM v4.1:  
"the obligation of the ICT third-party service provider to participate and fully cooperate in the financial entity’s TLPT."
analysis: STA-11 serves as a control that lists contractual provisions that are a must to have within a service agreement between CSP and CSC, and thus is a valid mapping. Partial gap is due to certain specificities/details on the provisions that must be included.

 "rights of access, inspection and audit by the financial entity, or an appointed third party, and by the competent authority, and the right to take copies of relevant documentation on-site if they are critical to the operations of the ICT third-party service provider, the effective exercise of which is not impeded or limited by other contractual arrangements or implementation policies."

source_description: The contractual arrangements on the use of ICT services supporting critical or important functions shall include, in addition to the elements referred to in paragraph 2, at least the right to monitor, on an ongoing basis, the ICT third-party service provider’s performance, which entails the right to agree on alternative assurance levels if other clients’ rights are affected;

source_description:
The contractual arrangements on the use of ICT services supporting critical or important functions shall include, in addition to the elements referred to in paragraph 2, at least the right to monitor, on an ongoing basis, the ICT third-party service provider’s performance, which entails the obligation to provide details on the scope, procedures to be followed and frequency of such inspections and audits;

By way of derogation from point (e), the ICT third-party service provider and the financial entity that is a microenterprise may agree that the financial entity's rights of access, inspection and audit can be delegated to an independent third party, appointed by the ICT third-party service provider, and that the financial entity is able to request information and assurance on the ICT third-party service provider's performance from the third party at any time.

source_description: The contractual arrangements on the use of ICT services supporting critical or important functions shall include, in addition to the elements referred to in paragraph 2, at least the exit strategies, in particular the establishment of a mandatory adequate transition period, during which the ICT third-party service provider will continue providing the respective functions, or ICT services, with a view to reducing the risk of disruption at the financial entity or to ensure its effective resolution and restructuring;
addendum:
Missing specification(s) in the CCM v4.1:  
"the establishment of a mandatory adequate transition period, during which the ICT third-party service provider will continue providing the respective functions, or ICT services, with a view to reducing the risk of disruption at the financial entity or to ensure its effective resolution and restructuring."
analysis: STA-11 calls out as part of contractual agreements both "service termination" as well as "operational resilience" provisions, which maps to this control. However, the specificity of the provision is not full covered, hence the partial gap.

source_description: Financial entities shall only make use of the services of an ICT third-party service provider established in a third country and which has been designated as critical in accordance with paragraph 1, point (a), if the latter has established a subsidiary in the Union within the 12 months following the designation.
addendum: Recommend that CCM uses the full DORA provision to close the gap. The mapped CCM controls cover in part the high specificity of the DORA provision objective.
analysis:
From a customer perspective, they must review and identify if such a designation applies to the prospective service provider, and if so, identify that there is a subsidiary in the EU. 

From a supplier perspective, if such a designation is made, ensure that the supplier-entity has or establishes a "subsidiary" in the EU. 

Note a related group company that is not a legal "subsidiary" will not suffice. The subsidiary should be in place no later than 12 months after the designation, in order to avoid the risk of losing customers mandated to cease using the supplier.

source_description: Financial entities may exchange amongst themselves cyber threat information and intelligence, including indicators of compromise, tactics, techniques, and procedures, cyber security alerts and configuration tools.

Financial entities may exchange amongst themselves cyber threat information and intelligence to the extent that such information and intelligence sharing aims to enhance the digital operational resilience of financial entities, in particular through raising awareness in relation to cyber threats, limiting or impeding the cyber threats’ ability to spread, supporting  defence capabilities, threat detection techniques, mitigation strategies or response and recovery stages;

Financial entities may exchange amongst themselves cyber threat information and intelligence to the extent that such information and intelligence sharing takes places within trusted communities of financial entities;

Financial entities may exchange amongst themselves cyber threat information and intelligence to the extent that such information and intelligence sharing  is implemented through information-sharing arrangements that protect the potentially sensitive nature of the information shared, and that are governed by rules of conduct in full respect of business confidentiality, protection of personal data in accordance with Regulation (EU) 2016/679 and guidelines on competition policy.
addendum: Recommend that CCM uses the full DORA provision to close the gap. The mapped CCM controls cover in part the high specificity of the DORA provision objective.
analysis:
DSP-01 covers "is implemented through information-sharing arrangements that protect the potentially sensitive nature of the information shared." 

GRC-07 covers "maintain policies and procedures for the classification, protection and handling of data...according to all applicable laws and regulations, standards, and risk level." 

HRS-10 covers "...and that are governed by rules of conduct in full respect of business confidentiality, protection of personal data in accordance with Regulation (EU) 2016/679 and guidelines on competition policy.
